nodes.label: Autonomous Run Playbook
nodes.rationale: You own the exit condition: define done as a checkable predicate before the first iteration, then drive to it without stopping. A plateau is not a stop, and the predicate is never relaxed to declare victory.

nodes.label: Autopilot-Full Playbook
nodes.rationale: You own the verdicts, never the PRs: one owner carries each PR from build to merge, and nothing merges until a swarm that never wrote the code has proven the code that lands. Green CI alone never authorizes a merge.

nodes.label: Babysit Playbook

nodes.label: Bug Fix Playbook

nodes.rationale: A failed action still shows the screen it re-observed, so the agent can re-aim from that screen.

nodes.label: ASSERTION_FAILED
nodes.rationale: At zero matches, assertions poll until the assertion timeout then raise ASSERTION_FAILED.

nodes.label: Locator filter()
nodes.rationale: Narrows a locator with hasText, hasNotText, has, hasNot; any other filter key or an empty filter({}) is INVALID_LOCATOR.

nodes.label: getByDisplayValue Query
nodes.rationale: Matches inputs by current value; on the web it cannot scope child queries or be a filter({ has }) or filter({ hasNot }) target.

nodes.label: getByLabel Query
nodes.rationale: Matches form controls by label; returns the innermost match.

nodes.label: getByPlaceholder Query
nodes.rationale: Matches inputs by placeholder.

nodes.label: getByRole Query
nodes.rationale: First choice locator: semantic role, optionally by accessible name and state.

nodes.label: getByTestId Query
nodes.rationale: Last resort locator: data-testid on the web, accessibility identifier or resource id on a device.

nodes.label: getByText Query
nodes.rationale: Matches visible text; returns the innermost match so a container echoing its child does not count twice.

nodes.label: INVALID_LOCATOR
nodes.rationale: Raised for an unsupported filter key or an empty filter({}).

nodes.label: LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS
nodes.rationale: Two matches fail at once under the exactly-one rule.

nodes.label: Locators
nodes.rationale: Lazy queries resolved by an action, read, or assertion; exactly one match required per action, read, or assertion.

nodes.label: screen Fixture (Screen)
nodes.rationale: Always available; screen.getBy* builds a lazy query resolved only by an action, read, or assertion.

nodes.label: scrollUntilVisible
nodes.rationale: Scrolls the viewport (down, slow by default) until the locator resolves visibly, else LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND.

nodes.label: COLLECTION_ERROR
nodes.rationale: A session name no setup declares fails before any app process starts, naming the declared sessions.

nodes.label: afterAll Hook
nodes.rationale: Runs on config.cleanupTimeout.

nodes.label: afterEach Hook
nodes.rationale: An afterEach that names a fixture whose setup failed is skipped.

nodes.label: app Fixture (App)
nodes.rationale: Always available; on a device it relaunches the pinned app, and a path opens as a link only when the target declares app.linkBase.

nodes.label: beforeAll Hook
nodes.rationale: Reruns per retry and per serial group (each a fresh module realm) on the test timeout; a failing beforeAll is a HOOK_FAILED run error skipping every test in its scope.

nodes.label: beforeEach Hook
nodes.rationale: On web, browser, app, and screen are test fixtures, so UI setup goes in beforeEach.

nodes.label: browser Fixture (Browser)
nodes.rationale: Browser targets only; import test from @e2e-dev/web.

nodes.label: desktop Fixture (Desktop)
nodes.rationale: Desktop targets only; import test from @e2e-dev/desktop.

nodes.label: device Fixture (Device)
nodes.rationale: Device targets only; import test from @e2e-dev/mobile; a device keeps its state between tests.

nodes.label: Fixtures
nodes.rationale: Fixtures are set up on demand; a fixture nothing names does not run unless declared auto.

nodes.label: HOOK_FAILED
nodes.rationale: A failing beforeAll is a HOOK_FAILED run error skipping every test in its scope.

nodes.label: Hooks
nodes.rationale: Hooks nest: outer beforeEach first, inner afterEach first; beforeAll reruns per retry and per serial group on the test timeout, afterAll runs on config.cleanupTimeout.

nodes.label: platform Fixture
nodes.rationale: Always available, hooks included; web, ios, android, or an engine's label.

nodes.label: Serial Groups
nodes.rationale: Serial members share app state, run in order on one worker, retry as a whole, and take the group's trace and video.

nodes.label: session Fixture (SetupSession)
nodes.rationale: Only available in test.setup.

nodes.label: test.extend
nodes.rationale: A test sets up the test.extend fixtures its body and its beforeEach/afterEach hooks name, and the ones those fixtures name; a cycle is COLLECTION_ERROR.

nodes.label: UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY
nodes.rationale: clearState() is UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY with connect.reconnectEndpoint or an attempt-scoped browser provider, and on a device with no pinned app both clearState and restart are.

nodes.label: Worker Fixture
nodes.rationale: Set up once per worker and target by the first test or suite hook that names it, torn down when the worker ends, and sees worker fixtures only; declare it in a module the test files import because a test file reloads after a failure and for each serial group and setup test.

nodes.label: describe
nodes.rationale: Nest a describe only to share a hook or an option (a session, agentContext, tags) with some of its tests; a file holds one feature.

nodes.label: describe.fail
nodes.rationale: Every test inside expected to fail; not on setup tests or on, inside, or around a serial group.

nodes.label: expect
nodes.rationale: expect pins what must be true at the end, and that check lets the replay cache rerun every goal before it later.

nodes.label: expect.poll
nodes.rationale: expect.poll and a plain-value expect confirm nothing for the replay cache, so end with a locator check too.

nodes.label: screen.getByRole
nodes.rationale: screen actions are for exact interactions and values.

nodes.label: toMatchSchema
nodes.rationale: Prefer it when the app already has a schema for the response.

nodes.label: Await every step call
nodes.rationale: Else STEP_NOT_AWAITED at the line of the call.

nodes.label: Focal Moment
nodes.rationale: The focal moment must come from this product and surface concept. A generic fade-and-rise, hover lift, parallax layer, or scroll reveal is not a thesis.

nodes.label: Motion Thesis
nodes.rationale: Write a short plan before implementation to ensure motion is purposeful and specific to the product.

nodes.label: prefers-reduced-motion
nodes.rationale: Reduced motion means fewer and gentler animations, not disabling all motion; feedback that confirms an action should remain legible.

nodes.label: Config Drift
nodes.rationale: The config is never auto-updated; the user decides whether to add uncovered files or switch to a glob.

nodes.label: CSP Detection
nodes.rationale: All CSP allowances are kept development-only, including manual middleware and meta-tag edits, so a deployed production site's CSP is never changed to load the localhost helper.

nodes.label: Framework Adapters
nodes.rationale: SvelteKit, Nuxt, and TanStack Start server-render their document shell, so a raw <script> in the entry template will not execute reliably; dedicated adapters are used instead.

nodes.label: Live Config (.impeccable/live/config.json)
nodes.rationale: Hard-excluded paths (**/node_modules/** and **/.git/**) cannot be overridden because injecting there would instrument third-party code.

nodes.label: Boundary validation
nodes.rationale: Parse once where data crosses in, then trust types inside; re-validating deep in call chains is wasted work.

nodes.label: Branded types
nodes.rationale: Validate once at the boundary; a brand comes from a verifying type guard, never from an as cast, so downstream code trusts the type.

nodes.label: Constructive modeling
nodes.rationale: Build the shape so the illegal value cannot be constructed, rather than relying on a runtime guard or a wish for refinement types.

nodes.label: Discriminated unions
nodes.rationale: A literal discriminant makes impossible state combinations unrepresentable, unlike a bag of optional fields.

nodes.label: Exhaustiveness checks
nodes.rationale: Assigning the discriminant to a never-typed local makes the compiler error when a new variant is added.

nodes.label: No as casts
nodes.rationale: Every as cast is a runtime crash waiting; cast only after the type system has verified the claim.

nodes.label: Object arguments
nodes.rationale: Object args make argument order self-documenting; skipped on hot paths where the allocation cost matters.

nodes.label: satisfies over as
nodes.rationale: satisfies validates the value without widening literal types.

nodes.label: Schema-derived types
nodes.rationale: Deriving from a generated schema type avoids a duplicate shape that drifts when the schema changes.

nodes.label: Schemas before hand-rolled guards
nodes.rationale: One schema owning validation avoids a schema, a duplicate interface, and a guard drifting apart.

nodes.label: Simplest total type
nodes.rationale: Strengthen a loose type only where it forces a non-null assertion, a cast, or a should-never-happen throw.

nodes.label: Type guards
nodes.rationale: A lying guard is worse than an as cast because the bug hides behind a name that says it is safe.

nodes.label: Comment Sicko
nodes.rationale: A read-only reviewer with a short keep list (license headers, public API doc comments, links explaining what code can't, behavior forced by an external dependency); everything else goes.

nodes.label: Build the Change and Clean the Diff
nodes.norm_label: build the change and clean the diff
nodes.rationale: The build playbooks share one discipline: say what you observed, and let the playbook demand the evidence. Cleanup is not optional polish — a padded diff reads as unfinished and the extra code is where the next bug hides.

nodes.label: /benchmark-checklist
nodes.rationale: A before-and-after number is the easiest evidence to get wrong by accident — a warm cache, a debug build on one side, or work outside the timed region can each produce a convincing speedup.

nodes.label: /unslop
nodes.rationale: Cleans slop out of prose (PR descriptions and commit bodies) rather than code.

nodes.label: /deslop
nodes.rationale: Removes narrating comments, unsupported guards, dead compatibility paths, and unrelated edits from code; ships in the cursor-team-kit plugin, not in pstack.

nodes.label: /no-comments
nodes.rationale: Comments need their own pass, and not from the agent that wrote them, because an author defends its comments the way you'd defend yours.

nodes.label: Bug Fix Playbook
nodes.rationale: Reproduce before fixing.

nodes.label: Feature Playbook
nodes.rationale: Name the data shape before implementing.

nodes.label: Hillclimb Playbook
nodes.rationale: For sustained improvement of one number: loops one hypothesis at a time with a frozen measurement harness, keeps wins and reverts everything else.

nodes.label: Opening a PR Playbook
nodes.rationale: Runs /deslop on the diff before each commit so the diff stays reviewable.

nodes.label: Perf Issue Playbook
nodes.rationale: Profile before optimizing; vets its baseline and every number after it with /benchmark-checklist.

nodes.label: Refactoring Playbook
nodes.rationale: Pin behavior before restructuring.

nodes.label: Runtime Forensics Playbook
nodes.rationale: Instruments the running process for a live symptom and returns a diagnosis, not a fix.

nodes.label: Trace Forensics Playbook
nodes.rationale: Reads an already-captured profile artifact and maps the hot frame to source; returns a diagnosis, not a fix.

nodes.label: /tdd
nodes.rationale: Writes the smallest test that fails for the intended reason, then the fix; if a test would need broad harness setup or brittle mocks it says so and uses the closest executable check instead.

nodes.label: /typescript-best-practices
nodes.rationale: Turns type-system principles into concrete rules but does not load on its own, so it must be named when a task touches .ts or .tsx files.

nodes.label: Cloud subagent
nodes.rationale: Each cloud subagent gets its own VM and branch, so it can install dependencies, run the app, and record video without touching the local machine.

nodes.label: "new task" task switch
nodes.rationale: Without it, a mode mid-Feature tends to treat a new question as the next feature step instead of re-matching the playbook.

nodes.label: What goes in a prompt (goal, done check, proof, known context, constraints)
nodes.norm_label: what goes in a prompt (goal, done check, proof, known context, constraints)
nodes.rationale: The how and the initial theory of the cause are deliberately left out: a prescribed path blocks better solutions and a stated guess narrows the search to wherever it points.

nodes.label: Worktree isolation for parallel work
nodes.rationale: Several agents against one repository on one machine fight over the working tree, ports, and build output; each task in its own branch and worktree prevents agents stomping each other's files, at the cost of disk and machine resources.

nodes.label: /figure-it-out
nodes.rationale: Used for large work or when no playbook matches; designs the run's phases for work reviewed later.

nodes.label: /in-your-own-words
nodes.rationale: Restating the goal and problem in the agent's own words surfaces a misreading before any code exists, costing one message instead of one wrong fix.

nodes.label: Opening a PR playbook
nodes.rationale: Already works from a worktree for code changes, so a worktree only needs to be requested when a specific base or location matters.

nodes.label: /poteto-mode
nodes.rationale: The playbook holds the structure and sequences the other skills, so prompts can stay short and hand-written skill sequences are discouraged.

nodes.label: /sharpen
nodes.rationale: Rewrites a prompt deeper but not bigger, asking the agent to prototype experiment-settleable choices while leaving product and preference choices to the user.

nodes.label: Worktree cleanup playbook
nodes.rationale: Classifies every worktree by merge state, uncommitted work, and which chats still touch it, deleting only what that evidence clears and pausing on uncommitted work.

nodes.label: browserstack()
nodes.rationale: appiumVersion must be set because BrowserStack's default Appium 1.x lacks mobile: commands.

nodes.label: e2b()
nodes.rationale: Runs Android 16 in one E2B sandbox per worker, so the runner needs no adb.

nodes.label: @e2e-dev/mobile
nodes.rationale: Pins agent-device exactly; each pin moves with its engine release.

nodes.label: expoSimulators()
nodes.rationale: Needs no Xcode or Android SDK, but a run must fit one session (maxDurationMinutes, else the account's cap).

nodes.label: mobile() engine
nodes.rationale: One worker per device, since two sessions on one device fight over it.

nodes.label: revyl()
nodes.rationale: Revyl devices record no video, so --video fails with UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY.

nodes.label: unstable_deviceSession()
nodes.rationale: Do not build a client yourself: it would miss the engine's daemon, lease, and session.

nodes.label: device.unstable_raw
nodes.rationale: Client calls are not steps: no report, trace, replay, or secret redaction; unstable and may change or go away in any release.

nodes.label: NODE_STALE
nodes.rationale: Returned before mutation when fields are missing or captures incomplete, then retried after a fresh observation.

nodes.label: Phase A: Frame
nodes.rationale: Rigor is gates and artifacts, not 'try harder'; one-way doors and high blast radius get more rigor, reversible low-stakes steps get less.

nodes.label: Phase B: Design the workflow
nodes.rationale: A second arena over a settled design is over-engineering; skip architect for mechanical work whose shape is already concrete.

nodes.label: Phase C: Run the loop
nodes.rationale: A verdict is VERIFIED, NOT VERIFIED, or INCONCLUSIVE; inconclusive is not a pass and a negative must not be hidden.

nodes.label: Phase D: Keep the audit trail
nodes.norm_label: phase d: keep the audit trail
nodes.rationale: The trail plus the diff is what lets the human come back and trust the work.

nodes.label: Phase E: Verify and hand back
nodes.norm_label: phase e: verify and hand back
nodes.rationale: Encode any recurring correction as a gate, lint rule, check, or script so the lesson becomes structure.

nodes.label: figure-it-out skill
nodes.rationale: When the task matches no playbook, design one: the deliverable before any code is the workflow itself, with a decision trail a human can audit after stepping away.

nodes.label: color-amount live-mode parameter
nodes.rationale: Lets the user move from neutral to the variant's full color strategy without regeneration.

nodes.label: Hero gate
nodes.rationale: Human review does not waive the hero gate's integrity checks.

nodes.label: OKLCH color space
nodes.rationale: Preferred for new web palettes because lightness and chroma can be adjusted predictably.

nodes.label: Semantic color tokens
nodes.rationale: Theme changes should normally remap semantic roles rather than primitive values.

nodes.label: Colorize Reference
nodes.rationale: Introduce color as hierarchy, meaning, and atmosphere while preserving confirmed brand and semantic conventions; do not replace a visual world under the guise of colorizing it.

nodes.label: Component Review Reference
nodes.rationale: A painted region planned as code is the most expensive mistake a comp-led build makes, so the user reviews plates and the production plan before page code exists.

nodes.label: Zoom and Text Scaling Preservation
nodes.rationale: Preserve browser zoom, user font settings, Dynamic Type, and platform text scaling so text remains usable.

nodes.label: Font Delivery and Fallbacks
nodes.rationale: Load only used assets and provide metric-compatible fallbacks to avoid invisible text and disruptive reflow.

nodes.label: Line Break Control (text-wrap balance/pretty)
nodes.rationale: Both properties are progressive: a browser that ignores them keeps its default wrap.

nodes.label: Live-Mode Scale Parameter
nodes.rationale: Every variant authors its type ramp against var(--p-scale, 1) so a single coarse scale parameter drives the ramp.

nodes.label: Mechanical Type Scan
nodes.rationale: A clean scan is a floor, not proof of good typography.

nodes.label: Reading Measure (45–75ch)
nodes.rationale: Tune line height inversely with measure: wider lines generally need more leading.

nodes.label: Type System (roles, contrast, measure)
nodes.rationale: Use the fewest roles and families that make the hierarchy unmistakable; combine size, weight, space, and tone instead of asking size alone to do all the work.

nodes.label: Typographic Assessment
nodes.rationale: Run independently of the mechanical scan so detector findings do not anchor the design assessment.

nodes.label: Visitor Mode
nodes.rationale: Persuade + Experience may let display type carry the voice; Operate + Read puts stability, scanability, and measure first; Native defers to platform guidance.

nodes.label: Typeset Reference
nodes.rationale: Typography carries information, hierarchy, and voice; improve it inside the established visual world rather than replacing the identity unless the user asked to.

nodes.label: Bounded cause tracing
nodes.rationale: The pass does not need a complete root cause, only enough to avoid routing a visible symptom to the wrong owner.

nodes.label: Report classification categories
nodes.rationale: When the bug versus feature line is unclear the run does not file; the single verdict may ask one focused question and use the other marker.

nodes.label: Tracker dedupe
nodes.rationale: A long-closed issue is treated as a regression lead, not automatically a live duplicate.

nodes.label: Fail-closed ticket creation
nodes.rationale: Prefer no ticket over a guessed or duplicate ticket; a missing or malformed config stops the run with no writes.

nodes.label: Issue-tracker adapter contract
nodes.rationale: The tracker is an adapter rather than a required vendor so Linear, GitHub Issues, or another tracker can implement the same operations.

nodes.label: Read-only delegated workers
nodes.rationale: The coordinator is the only Slack poster, so delegated workers return findings only and receive no Slack credentials or write actions.

nodes.label: Configured routing map
nodes.rationale: A visible symptom alone is not enough to route when cause tracing points elsewhere, so routes match on confirmed product area, code path, or error signature.

nodes.label: Immutable source coordinates
nodes.rationale: Freezing SOURCE_CHANNEL_ID and SOURCE_THREAD_TS before any work keeps every later read and post on the original thread and prevents a reply timestamp from replacing the root.

nodes.label: Verdict marker contract
nodes.rationale: The repro automation trusts the marker only when it comes from the configured triage identity in the source thread, so exactly one marker line ends the verdict.

nodes.label: Routing map example
nodes.rationale: The example is copied outside the pack directory so pack refreshes do not overwrite a team's real routing map.

nodes.label: Unslop skill
nodes.rationale: Rule numbers are stable ids that other skills cite, so a removed rule leaves a gap.

nodes.label: Why skill
nodes.rationale: Answers from the record rather than the code, citing what authors wrote and marking inferences as inferences.

nodes.label: npm run guard:flow
nodes.rationale: The guard run sets noInlineConfig and allows no warnings, so no comment can switch a guard off.

nodes.label: Framework map (need → tool feature → exact doc page)
nodes.norm_label: framework map (need → tool feature → exact doc page)
nodes.rationale: A top-level site, search result or llms.txt is not the cited job page; llms.txt is only the index used to find that page.

nodes.label: Evidence
nodes.rationale: No Evidence means not done.

nodes.label: Proof
nodes.rationale: Any source change makes proof stale.

nodes.label: Proof story
nodes.rationale: A card that needs more than one drive to prove is too big and splits.

nodes.label: Rehearsal copy
nodes.rationale: Real Julia is never involved.

nodes.label: Test data
nodes.rationale: Set up once; never Real Julia's data.

nodes.label: UAT
nodes.rationale: Only things a user would do; technical checking is the robot's job and happens before UAT.

nodes.label: Decision log (decisions.tsv)
nodes.rationale: One change, one check, one log row per iteration makes an unattended run auditable in the morning; it stays local unless the work is ambitious enough that a reviewer needs the trail.

nodes.label: Checkable finish condition
nodes.rationale: A duration is not a finish condition: 'work on this for 4 hours' gives the agent nothing to check, so the loop needs a predicate that can pass or fail.

nodes.label: Morning audit
nodes.rationale: Auditing decisions rather than re-reading the whole night keeps review cheap; the Attention section points at what deserves scrutiny first.

nodes.label: Scheduled or event-driven automation
nodes.rationale: Every stage can stop the line and every stage hands over evidence, so bad work does not reach a later stage where it costs more to undo.

nodes.label: Verification swarm
nodes.rationale: No owner merges on its own verdict; only a clean verdict on the patch that merges authorizes the merge, and a full swarm is re-run only for new behavior or a large new diff.

nodes.label: Autopilot-stack playbook
nodes.rationale: Autopilot-stack is Autopilot-full without the merge, chosen when you want your own eyes on the work before anything merges.

nodes.label: Optional ai Package
nodes.rationale: Optional: without it sessions open and the deterministic tools work, so no model is needed.

nodes.label: open_session
nodes.rationale: A session runs the test and stops where it failed, so a fix does not need to walk the flow again from the start over call.

nodes.label: screenshot
nodes.rationale: Masks secure fields only, after a secret fill too.

nodes.label: CONFIG_IN_USE
nodes.rationale: Open sessions use another config, or were opened with engine and this one names a config; open the same way or close them first.

nodes.label: ENGINE_IN_USE
nodes.rationale: The target's engine comes from a package every session shares; create it in the config or a file it imports by path.

nodes.label: SESSION_OPEN
nodes.rationale: Every session slot is taken; close one or raise --max-sessions.

nodes.label: TEST_AMBIGUOUS
nodes.rationale: The test name must select one test on the session's target; several matches are listed as file:line.

nodes.label: actions/upload-artifact
nodes.rationale: Upload artifacts unless cancelled, so a test that failed then passed on retry keeps its evidence.

nodes.label: decisionFilter
nodes.rationale: Filters run only with --changed-since <ref>; every test runs without it and on a --last-failed rerun. The decision filter also runs every test on a lockfile or e2e.config change, and the tests whose test file, setup file, or stored screenshots changed. With one worker (the CI default) only the relevance bands order files and collection order breaks ties.

nodes.label: Install Playwright Browsers
nodes.rationale: Install browsers as their own step so the download stays out of the launch timeout.

nodes.label: Target app.command
nodes.rationale: Start the app through the target's app.command; the runner tears it down on every exit path.

nodes.label: .e2e/cache/
nodes.rationale: Commit .e2e/cache/ so recorded steps replay with no model call.

nodes.label: Impeccable Commands
nodes.rationale: Only recommend commands from the approved list, ending with $impeccable polish as the final step if any fixes are recommended.

nodes.label: $impeccable polish
nodes.rationale: Always the final step when any fixes were recommended.

nodes.label: Amplification
nodes.rationale: A flat section is typically one that quietly opts out of the system's own strongest moves; bring it up to the expressive level its neighbors already reach.

nodes.label: Bolder Command
nodes.rationale: The reflex answer, reaching for more effects, is the opposite of bold; reject it first.

nodes.label: Open Direction Round
nodes.rationale: An open direction round owns the word first; 'bolder' during a direction decision is a fresh deal of foreign forms, not this command.

nodes.label: Scope Is Sovereign
nodes.rationale: Everything else stays is a literal instruction; do not restyle neighbors or expand the system on your own.

nodes.label: Skeleton Test
nodes.rationale: If it only works once the words return, the boldness is in the text size, not the design.

nodes.label: Heuristic 9: Help Users Recognize, Diagnose, and Recover from Errors
nodes.norm_label: heuristic 9: help users recognize, diagnose, and recover from errors

nodes.label: Priority Issues
nodes.rationale: Prioritize ruthlessly: if everything is important, nothing is.

nodes.label: Fluid Typography with clamp()
nodes.rationale: Set minimum readable sizes (16px body on mobile); iOS Safari force-zooms focused inputs under 16px, which breaks form layouts.

nodes.label: Flex/Grid Overflow Prevention (min-width: 0)
nodes.rationale: Allow shrinking below content size.

nodes.label: Interface Hardening
nodes.rationale: Designs that only work with perfect data aren't production-ready.

nodes.label: Interrupted Gestures (Pointer Cancel Handling)
nodes.rationale: A second finger or pointer lands mid-drag: the first drag keeps its pointer or ends cleanly, never jumps to the new one.

nodes.label: Real Constraints
nodes.rationale: Constraints such as "repro first" or "let me review before proceeding" each change what the agent does.

nodes.label: Design Before the Plan
nodes.rationale: Reviewers of an abstract plan invent risks that never happen, so let prototypes answer the open questions instead.

nodes.label: Done Check
nodes.rationale: A check must be able to pass or fail; "make it better" and a duration are not checks.

nodes.label: Follow Up Short
nodes.rationale: Once the chat holds the task, "do it" or "keep going until done" are whole prompts; "new task" is needed when the subject changes or the mode treats the message as the next step.

nodes.label: Leave Out the How
nodes.rationale: Say what to achieve and leave the agent room to find a better way; a hand-written step order drops or reorders steps the playbook keeps.

nodes.label: Load the Context First
nodes.rationale: An agent with no traced model fixes the symptom at the first plausible spot; a misreading shows up before any code exists.

nodes.label: Steer in One Line
nodes.rationale: A principle name works because the agent already read the rule; its reply names the decision the rule changed.

nodes.label: The Estimate Rule
nodes.rationale: A dollar figure never appears without the word estimate beside it; a percentage appears with the window it belongs to and that window's own reset date.

nodes.label: The Flat Papers Rule
nodes.rationale: Cards do not hover, lift, or gain shadow on interaction, because nothing on this screen is interactive; depth comes from colour and edge, never from motion.

nodes.label: Helper card
nodes.rationale: The action list scrolls inside 15rem rather than growing the page.

nodes.label: The larder (creative north star)
nodes.rationale: Bottle green carries the header and run panel, sage is the ground, ivory cards hold the detail, so the screen reads like a chalked board in a well-stocked kitchen rather than a developer console.

nodes.label: The One Display Rule
nodes.rationale: Exactly one thing on the screen is display size: the stage the run is in; card titles and section titles never compete with it.

nodes.label: Quota row
nodes.rationale: A low window is ringed as well as coloured; an unknown reading shows no number, no stale value, and no warning.

nodes.label: The Red For Trouble Rule
nodes.rationale: Madder red marks a problem and nothing else; it never decorates a heading, a link, or a bar that is healthy.

nodes.label: Stage rail
nodes.rationale: Future stages are not drawn; the rail grows as the machine reaches each stage, so the rail is a record, not a plan.

nodes.label: Step row
nodes.rationale: Labels are cut to their first sentence and 42 characters so the row stays a row; the full name stays on the step line below.

nodes.label: Warning banner
nodes.rationale: A banner says what is wrong and never suggests a fix.

nodes.label: Mission control design system
nodes.rationale: The system reports, it does not sell: no primary action, no chart, no table; problems are the only place madder red appears and every problem has a shape as well as a colour so the screen still tells the truth in grey print or to a colour-blind eye.

nodes.label: continue
nodes.rationale: Straight to the network; a header set to undefined is dropped, the configured headers still added on an allowed origin.

nodes.label: fallback
nodes.rationale: The route registered before it.

nodes.label: route
nodes.rationale: Intercept requests, newest route first; pattern is a URL pattern or { method, url } for one method.

nodes.label: credentials
nodes.rationale: Secrets never appear in test code; accounts are declared in config and resolved as opaque values.

nodes.label: e2e MCP server
nodes.rationale: Writing the test while walking the flow over MCP avoids the one-failure-per-run cost of writing it from memory afterwards.

nodes.label: secrets
nodes.rationale: Separate namespace from credentials so secrets.get never returns a password.

nodes.label: Operate Comps
nodes.rationale: A comp an engineer could not build from the platform's standard components is a picture of the tool, not the tool.

nodes.label: Signature Move
nodes.rationale: The signature move adds to a screen that is already clean; it never stands in for the finish bar.

nodes.label: World Contributions (type, palette, density, signature move)
nodes.norm_label: world contributions (type, palette, density, signature move)
nodes.rationale: The world lends only type, palette, density and one signature move; it never supplies the layout, navigation model or controls, so a working screen never reads as a costume.

nodes.label: Product Color
nodes.rationale: Product defaults to Restrained; accent color is reserved for primary actions, current selection, and state indicators, not decoration.

nodes.label: Product Components
nodes.rationale: Every interactive component needs default, hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, and error states; overlays must escape clipping ancestors.

nodes.label: Product Layout
nodes.rationale: Responsive behavior is structural, not fluid typography.

nodes.label: Product Motion
nodes.rationale: Users are in flow; don't make them wait for choreography. Motion conveys state, not decoration.

nodes.label: Product Constraints
nodes.rationale: Modals are usually laziness; exhaust inline and progressive alternatives first.

nodes.label: Product Permissions
nodes.rationale: Consistency over surprise: the same visual vocabulary screen to screen is a virtue; delight is saved for moments, not pages.

nodes.label: Product Slop Test
nodes.rationale: Product UI's failure mode isn't flatness, it's strangeness without purpose. The bar is earned familiarity; the tool should disappear into the task.

nodes.label: Product Typography
nodes.rationale: Product UIs don't need display/body pairing; a fixed rem scale and tighter ratio serve consistent-DPI task views better than fluid type.

nodes.label: Experience mode
nodes.rationale: The visitor is inside the work itself; let the artifact lead from the first viewport and let the interface recede.

nodes.label: Operate mode
nodes.rationale: The visitor completes a task; scanability, consistency, native expectations, and the real usage scene outrank expression.

nodes.label: Persuade mode
nodes.rationale: The visitor decides and acts; design is the product. Landing pages, marketing, campaigns, pricing.

nodes.label: Read mode
nodes.rationale: The visitor understands something; structure for comprehension, then make the reading experience worth staying in.

nodes.label: impeccable skill
nodes.rationale: Refinement preserves the incumbent identity, behavior, copy, and everything outside scope; redesign keeps product truth but treats the old look as evidence and anti-reference. Visual authority is evidence, not a filename.

nodes.label: HIG conformance
nodes.rationale: HIG conformance governs structure, navigation, and interaction in every mode; brand expresses through the layer the platform leaves open (tint, type, motion, content).

nodes.label: Design Before You Write Code
nodes.rationale: The two most common design mistakes are taking the agent's first design and polishing a plan that no code has tested; this page fixes both by planning through code — prototypes answer open questions, a README or tutorial sets the target, and the written plan comes last.

nodes.label: /technical-writing
nodes.rationale: Named when the doc itself matters, so a tutorial stays a tutorial instead of drifting into reference and explanation at once.

nodes.label: /arena
nodes.rationale: Gives every worker the same brief and merges the best parts.

nodes.label: /swarm
nodes.rationale: Splits work into slices or a race and returns one report.

nodes.label: Technical writing
nodes.rationale: Layered standard (Diátaxis mode, Google developer style, STE sentence rules, Global English) so a tired engineer understands on the first read.

nodes.label: /architect
nodes.rationale: Settles types and boundaries before implementation: traces every system the change touches, sketches two shapes, and picks the one where each piece of state has one owner, each task has one way to do it, and callers need to know least.

nodes.label: /arena
nodes.rationale: N subagents attempt the same brief in parallel in separate worktrees; a read-only cross-vendor judge scores candidates against a rubric, then the coordinator picks a base, grafts the best ideas from losers, and verifies.

nodes.label: /interrogate
nodes.rationale: A finding survives only when rerunning its command shows a failure that breaks the intent, so adversaries are wasted on an abstract plan with no code to break.

nodes.label: Multi-phase Plan Playbook
nodes.rationale: pstack has no planning skill on purpose; a written plan is requested only once the design is settled, and each PR section ends in proof that the change works — a passing test suite alone doesn't count.

nodes.label: Prototype Playbook
nodes.rationale: Prototypes are planning with code: they let the agent answer its own open questions by running something instead of asking, and leave room for an option you wouldn't have thought of.

nodes.label: /setup-pstack
nodes.rationale: Supplies the configured model panel that /arena draws its candidates from.

nodes.label: /swarm
nodes.rationale: Used when parallelism buys coverage or lets independent checks race; it does not use the base-selection and grafting ceremony of /arena.

nodes.label: call
nodes.rationale: Each action prints the Test line that repeats it; where it differs from the test's line, use the printed one.

nodes.label: observe
nodes.rationale: Before a long run, observe once to reset the idle clock so the session does not close and stop the app under the run.

nodes.label: run_code
nodes.rationale: The code is parsed, never evaluated as JavaScript, so only a fixed statement grammar runs; secrets may only go into fill under type_secret's checks.

nodes.label: test_lines
nodes.rationale: A line's locator matched the target alone on the live screen before the action, so the draft test body is unambiguous.

nodes.label: type_secret
nodes.rationale: The plaintext never reaches the agent; its test line names the credential or secret instead of the value.

nodes.label: Font Scale / Dark Mode Verification Commands
nodes.norm_label: font scale / dark mode verification commands
nodes.rationale: Dark theme and font scale belong in the review pass; a 1.3 font scale catches clipped labels a fixed layout hides, and settings must be read first and restored after.

nodes.label: Android Slop Test
nodes.rationale: The most common tell of an untrustworthy Android app is an iOS app wearing Android's skin — bottom-only navigation, back arrows ignoring the system Back gesture, Cupertino-shaped switches and dialogs.

nodes.label: Dark Theme
nodes.rationale: Dark theme is a first-class scheme to design and test; never a quick invert.

nodes.label: Dynamic Color (Material You)
nodes.rationale: Derives the scheme from the user's wallpaper on Android 12+, with a static fallback.

nodes.label: Floating Action Button (FAB)
nodes.rationale: One FAB, one primary action — never stack FABs or spend one on a secondary task.

nodes.label: Material Color Roles
nodes.rationale: Role tokens (primary, on-primary, surface, surface-variant, secondary-container, outline, error) resolve light/dark and contrast variants automatically; raw hex breaks there.

nodes.label: Material Design 3
nodes.rationale: Material Design 3 governs structure, navigation, and interaction in every mode; brand expresses through Material's theming (color roles, type scale, shape, motion).

nodes.label: Material Motion Patterns
nodes.rationale: Container transform, shared-axis, and fade-through with standard easing and durations; the system Remove animations setting is honored with a crossfade or instant cut.

nodes.label: Material Type Scale
nodes.rationale: Text maps to Display/Headline/Title/Body/Label roles rather than hand-picked per-screen sizes; sp units are used so type follows the system font-size setting.

nodes.label: Material Navigation Bar / Rail / Drawer
nodes.rationale: Navigation must be matched to window size: bottom navigation bar (3–5 destinations) on compact width, rail or drawer on expanded width; a phone bottom-bar must never ship untouched on a tablet.

nodes.label: Snackbar
nodes.rationale: Snackbars carry transient feedback (actionable when useful); dialogs are reserved for decisions that must interrupt.

nodes.label: Tonal Elevation
nodes.rationale: Elevation is conveyed through standard surface tonal levels (plus shadow where appropriate); no arbitrary drop shadows.

nodes.label: impeccable live-server
nodes.rationale: Startup requeues unacknowledged events, so the user never has to click Go again after a helper restart.

nodes.label: Live Session Journal
nodes.rationale: The append-only journal under .impeccable/live/sessions/ is canonical durable state and replays unacknowledged work after a helper restart.

nodes.label: Roots Manifest
nodes.rationale: Every helper re-anchors to the persisted manifest at startup so a wrong cwd cannot fork session state.

nodes.label: Test Fixtures (tests/fixtures.ts)
nodes.rationale: Preferred over a bare seed test because pushing navigation into a fixture lets scenario tests reuse it.

nodes.label: Generated Playwright TypeScript
nodes.rationale: Every playwright-cli action emits the equivalent Playwright TypeScript, and that generated code is the raw material for every test.

nodes.label: tracing-start
nodes.rationale: Start tracing before the problem so the entire flow is captured, not just the failing step.

nodes.label: disposable.dispose
nodes.rationale: Used to remove a sticky overlay that was added without a duration.

nodes.label: page.screencast.showChapter
nodes.rationale: Full-screen chapter card with blurred backdrop, blocks until duration expires then auto-removes — ideal for section transitions.

nodes.label: page.screencast.showOverlay
nodes.rationale: Overlays are pointer-events: none, so they do not interfere with page interactions and can safely stay visible while clicking, filling, or performing actions.

nodes.label: Manual Assertions
nodes.rationale: Generated code captures actions but not assertions, so expectations must be added manually.

nodes.label: Debug CLI Attach Session (--debug=cli + attach tw-XXXX)
nodes.norm_label: debug cli attach session (--debug=cli + attach tw-xxxx)
nodes.rationale: Attaching to the paused test captures any custom setup done in the test, which simply opening the app URL would miss.

nodes.label: Generate Phase
nodes.rationale: The live app is the source of truth; editing the spec mid-generation is expected when it is vague or stale.

nodes.label: Heal Phase
nodes.rationale: Failures are fixed one at a time because shared state and the single CLI session make parallel fixes fragile.

nodes.label: Plan → Generate → Heal Workflow
nodes.rationale: Plan, generate and heal all lean on the same mechanic: run `npx playwright test --debug=cli` in the background, then attach with `playwright-cli attach tw-XXXX` to drive the paused page interactively.

nodes.label: Planning Phase
nodes.rationale: Goal is to produce a spec file enumerating scenarios; the spec must always be written to a file.

nodes.label: Seed Test
nodes.rationale: `--debug=cli` pauses inside the seed test, so the seed is where every planning and generation session begins; scenarios assume a fresh start after the seed.

nodes.label: Semantic Locators
nodes.rationale: Role-based locators are more resilient than fragile CSS selectors.

nodes.label: Trace vs Video vs Screenshot
nodes.rationale: Traces are best for debugging because they support DOM inspection, network details and step-by-step replay, unlike video or screenshots.

nodes.label: Tracing
nodes.rationale: Traces capture DOM snapshots, screenshots, network activity and console logs for debugging and analysis.

nodes.label: Hero Script Recording
nodes.rationale: Recording an entire scripted scenario via run-code allows inserting appropriate pauses between actions and annotating the video, which is preferred when producing a video for the user or as proof of work.

nodes.label: Attach to Running Browser
nodes.rationale: Attach connects to an already-running browser instead of launching a new one; detach leaves the external browser running.

nodes.label: Browser Session
nodes.rationale: Named sessions isolate cookies, storage, cache, history and tabs so multiple flows can run concurrently.

nodes.label: Element Ref
nodes.rationale: By default, use refs from the snapshot to interact with page elements.

nodes.label: Raw Output
nodes.rationale: The --raw option strips status, generated code and snapshot sections so output can be piped into other tools.

nodes.label: run-code Command
nodes.rationale: Use run-code to execute arbitrary Playwright code for advanced scenarios not covered by CLI commands.

nodes.label: Snapshot
nodes.rationale: Snapshots are preferred over screenshots because they are more common and cheaper to inspect.

nodes.label: Storage State
nodes.rationale: Saving and restoring storage state lets later sessions skip login.

nodes.label: Spec File (specs/<feature>.plan.md)
nodes.rationale: Each scenario is independent and starts from the seed's fresh state — never chain scenarios.

nodes.label: trace-{timestamp}.network
nodes.rationale: Complete network activity including headers, bodies, timing breakdown and failed requests.

nodes.label: resources/ Directory
nodes.rationale: Cached resources (images, fonts, stylesheets, scripts, response bodies) needed to reconstruct page state for replay.

nodes.label: trace-{timestamp}.trace
nodes.rationale: Main action log: every action, DOM snapshots before/after, screenshots, timing, console messages and source locations.

nodes.label: Render a Chart Reference
nodes.rationale: Pele's defaults are smaller than a chart of 500 states can be, so pass larger limits.

nodes.label: Statechart Skill
nodes.rationale: Aim for about 20 arrows or fewer, because a busier chart is hard to read.

nodes.label: e2e feedback
nodes.rationale: Reports are limited to e2e's own reproducible problems, dry-run first and sent only with user agreement, to avoid noise and leaking app content.

nodes.label: npx e2e guide
nodes.rationale: Prints the installed package's version of a reference, which is preferred when it differs from this copy.

nodes.label: Progressive Disclosure
nodes.rationale: Don't show everything at once on mobile; prioritize primary content.

nodes.label: Design Simplification (Distill)
nodes.rationale: Simplicity is not about removing features. It's about removing obstacles between users and their goals. Every element should justify its existence.

nodes.label: Kicker / Eyebrow Ban
nodes.rationale: This one is a ban, not a default: no brief earns it back. The heading carries its own weight; delete the label and let the heading speak.

nodes.label: Page Scaffolds Refusal
nodes.rationale: These are the category's defaults, not bans: the brief's own words can earn any of them. Reaching for one when the axis is free means you were not deciding; recognizing that means rewriting the element, not softening it.

nodes.label: Surface Habits Refusal
nodes.rationale: These are the category's defaults, not bans: the brief's own words can earn any of them. Reaching for one when the axis is free means you were not deciding; recognizing that means rewriting the element, not softening it.

nodes.label: impeccable build-phase finish
nodes.rationale: Records the final review disposition; a refused ship is an unfinished build, and any edit after the last captured gate voids that capture.

nodes.label: impeccable comp-diff
nodes.rationale: Produces side-by-side, heatmap, paired region crops, and report.json; the side-by-side is the view the build thread never has on its own.

nodes.label: impeccable detect
nodes.rationale: On hookless web builds, run once on changed targets and fix mechanical findings; a native platform skips the detector entirely.

nodes.label: impeccable-finish-reviewer agent
nodes.rationale: Spawned fresh with no forked conversation history so it does not inherit the build thread's framing, optimism, and abstractions.

nodes.label: Capture validity
nodes.rationale: A capture is evidence only when valid: settle or disable entrance motion, capture from the document top, and open every file to confirm it shows what its name claims.

nodes.label: Fix disposition
nodes.rationale: Apply the material fixes in one batch, rebuild once, and recapture the same viewports over the same files.

nodes.label: Rebuild disposition
nodes.rationale: Fidelity failed wholesale, not in patches; re-derive the named regions, produce the named assets, and send the result back for a fresh full review.

nodes.label: Recapture disposition
nodes.rationale: The evidence failed, not the build; a review conducted on invalid evidence binds nothing and a verdict pass may never follow it.

nodes.label: Ship disposition
nodes.rationale: Nothing is owed; report the verdict at its scope and continue to the documenter.

nodes.label: Responsive phase
nodes.rationale: The first viewport must hold at common desktop widths, not only at the comp's exact size; a displaced region is restored by resizing what sits above it, not by moving it alone.

nodes.label: Mastra Studio
nodes.rationale: A card begins in Mastra Studio's run form and nowhere else; no script starts one.

nodes.label: scripts/check-agent-brief.mjs
nodes.rationale: Enforces triage's 'behavioral, not procedural' brief rule so acceptance criteria describe what Todd needs.

nodes.label: Feature map
nodes.rationale: The map is the project's maintained verification source and the bug bash reads its charters; a proof that drives one convenient entry point is incomplete when the map lists others, and a bug bash that skips a mapped feature reports the gap.

nodes.label: Priority Order
nodes.rationale: Fix broken or blocked tasks first, then missing states, then flow and design-system drift, then visual and motion inconsistencies, then code and asset cleanup.

nodes.label: Triage
nodes.rationale: Triage writes the card shape (short Outcome plus acceptance criteria describing what Todd sees) and runs the writing-for-agents script before showing Todd a brief.

nodes.label: Maintain Verification Skill
nodes.rationale: A feature map rots the moment the app changes.

nodes.label: Live Action Vocabulary
nodes.rationale: Direction wording maps onto the live action vocabulary; a new action value is never invented.

nodes.label: impeccable (intent-carrying action)
nodes.rationale: Wording that carries intent but no vocabulary word maps to impeccable with the user's wording passed as the prompt.

nodes.label: Density Parameter
nodes.rationale: Every live-mode variant declares a coarse density range and authors spacing against var(--p-density, 1) so density stays tunable without re-authoring layout.

nodes.label: Layout Assessment
nodes.rationale: Run independently from the mechanical scan so that hierarchy and rhythm are judged on rendered or source evidence, not on detector output.

nodes.label: Mechanical Scan
nodes.rationale: A clean scan cannot prove hierarchy or rhythm, so mechanical evidence is kept out of the first assessment and synthesized afterwards.

nodes.label: Documented Spacing Scale
nodes.rationale: A 4-unit base usually provides the useful middle steps that an 8-only scale misses; one-off values erode rhythm.

nodes.label: Spatial Thesis
nodes.rationale: Naming the reading path, groupings, lead/support roles, density, and adaptation before editing forces the simplest structural model that expresses the relationships.

nodes.label: Squint Test
nodes.rationale: With detail blurred, the primary element, secondary element, and major groups should still be identifiable in order.

nodes.label: Layout Reference
nodes.rationale: Layout turns product priority into reading order, grouping, rhythm, and usable space; the structural problem must be diagnosed before moving boxes.

nodes.label: Operate + Read Mode
nodes.rationale: The tool should disappear more completely into the task.

nodes.label: Plan Refinement
nodes.rationale: Subtlety requires precision. Quiet without intent collapses to generic.

nodes.label: Quiet Design
nodes.rationale: Quiet design is harder than bold design; subtlety needs precision. Reduce visual intensity without losing personality or making the result generic.

nodes.label: Visitor Mode (Persuade + Experience)
nodes.rationale: Drama is reduced, not eliminated; the POV stays intact.

nodes.label: Comp crops
nodes.rationale: Comp crops are reference evidence only, never production assets.

nodes.label: Principle: Build the Lever
nodes.rationale: The tool is the artifact a reviewer can rerun, so building it beats working by hand; the bar for skipping is triviality, not repetition.

nodes.label: Principle: Encode Lessons in Structure
nodes.rationale: If the fix is structural, only the structural fix should be used; the instruction is the symptom.

nodes.label: Principle: Guard the Context Window
nodes.rationale: Context overflow degrades reasoning quality, creates compression artifacts, and halts progress.

nodes.label: Principle: Prove It Works
nodes.rationale: Proxies such as file mtimes, self-reports, cached output, and 'it compiles' do not count as verification; when a check fails, suspect the observation method before the system.

nodes.label: Principle: Sequence Verifiable Units
nodes.rationale: Ordering delivery so the sequence proves itself (failing test first, subtraction before reshape, baseline before treatment) makes the work verifiable to a reviewer.

nodes.label: Principle: Test Behavior, Not Implementation
nodes.rationale: A test should fail when observable behavior breaks and keep passing when only internals change; otherwise it proves nothing or is pinned to the implementation.

nodes.label: Skill: Recall
nodes.rationale: A feature with a long bug tail keeps most of its story in the shared record (source control, issue tracker, chat, docs, error tracking), so context must not be reconstructed from transcripts alone.

nodes.label: Skill: Reflect
nodes.rationale: A finding is only kept if it will still hold in six months, would change what a future agent does, and routes to a skill the session used; what a lint, script or check could enforce goes to the backlog, not into prose.

nodes.label: "Convince me" framing
nodes.rationale: Turns an explanation into an argument you can test instead of a tour, and forces the agent to read the code and back each claim with evidence.

nodes.label: Read-only investigation (findings, not a fix)
nodes.rationale: Asking for findings plus the data used makes the agent separate evidence from guesses; the fix then starts as a new task.

nodes.label: read-only general-purpose subagent
nodes.rationale: One read-only subagent explores and explains in one pass so the user gets a senior-engineer mental model without the main agent rewriting it.

nodes.label: Understand the code before changing it
nodes.norm_label: understand the code before changing it
nodes.rationale: Agents fail either by misreading intent or by lacking context; this page addresses the context half, because editing code you don't understand is how subtle regressions ship.

nodes.label: /how
nodes.rationale: Explains what the code does now at senior-engineer onboarding level, using one read-only subagent to explore and write the explanation.

nodes.label: Investigation playbook
nodes.rationale: Traces the code, adds /why for motivation questions, and returns a cited explanation or a recommendation with a trade-offs table.

nodes.label: /recall
nodes.rationale: Old chats hold context a fresh agent lacks, so new work on an old topic starts by loading that context first.

nodes.label: Session pickup playbook
nodes.rationale: Treats the prior trail as authoritative: reconstructs branch state and decisions, names the resume point, and verifies inherited claims against the original goal instead of re-deriving everything.

nodes.label: /teach
nodes.rationale: For when a summary isn't enough: it weaves /how and /why into a plain explanation built diagram by diagram, forcing the agent to back each claim with evidence.

nodes.label: /why
nodes.rationale: Answers from the record (commits, PR discussions) rather than the code, marks its own inferences as inferences, and treats "nobody wrote down why" as itself an answer.

nodes.label: how skill
nodes.rationale: Explains subsystem architecture, runtime flow, and onboarding mental models; use why for motivation.

nodes.label: credentials config
nodes.rationale: Credentials live in the config, values in the environment; a static password or secret needs 6 or more code points so an unset variable fails every command.

nodes.label: credentials.user()
nodes.rationale: Outside a run it throws AUTH_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE.

nodes.label: fill
nodes.rationale: A function password is read at fill time and redacted only from that fill on.

nodes.label: pressSequentially
nodes.rationale: Use when the app reacts to keystrokes (autocomplete, masked input); fill sets the value with no key events.

nodes.label: Secret
nodes.rationale: A Secret has no plaintext accessor, is named to the agent and in reports, and stringifying it is INVALID_CONFIG; only fill() and agent.act params accept it.

nodes.label: secrets config and secrets.get()
nodes.rationale: Any other sensitive value is a secrets entry; secrets.get() never returns a credential password (separate namespaces).

nodes.label: E2E_USER_* and E2E_SECRET_* overrides
nodes.rationale: Override either field per run, even over a function; two credentials or secrets mapping to one variable are INVALID_CONFIG.

nodes.label: Aha Moment
nodes.rationale: Getting users to the moment that proves the product is worth their time is the measure of onboarding success.

nodes.label: Contextual Tooltips
nodes.rationale: Teach features at the point of use, when users need them, rather than upfront.

nodes.label: Empty States
nodes.rationale: Empty states are onboarding opportunities: they should teach the interface rather than show blank space.

nodes.label: Guided Tours and Walkthroughs
nodes.rationale: Tours should focus on workflow, not features, and stay short (3-7 steps) so users can explore freely.

nodes.label: Onboarding Implementation Patterns
nodes.rationale: Show onboarding once: track completion and respect dismissals.

nodes.label: Interactive Tutorials
nodes.rationale: High-stakes or unfamiliar concepts are better practiced in a safe sandbox environment.

nodes.label: Onboarding
nodes.rationale: Onboarding's job is not to teach the product. Its job is to get people to the moment that proves the product is worth their time.

nodes.label: Verify Onboarding Quality
nodes.rationale: Test with real users on time to completion, comprehension, action, skip rate, completion rate, and time to value.

nodes.label: Time to Value
nodes.rationale: Front-load the most important concepts and teach the 20% that delivers 80% of value.

nodes.label: Bring Up Capability
nodes.rationale: The adapter must distinguish the target app from a similar window, shell, or production instance.

nodes.label: Cleanup Capability
nodes.rationale: Cleanup must not delete user work.

nodes.label: Drive Mapped Features Capability
nodes.rationale: Arranging a precondition is not permission to inject the reported symptom; the repro itself must still come from real user interaction.

nodes.label: Drive UI Capability
nodes.rationale: Do not set internal state, call hidden app methods, write directly to storage, or inject DOM changes to create the symptom.

nodes.label: Environment Translation
nodes.rationale: Use a translated attempt only when it tests the same underlying behavior; do not call it an exact repro when the missing environment is part of the defect.

nodes.label: Inspect State Capability
nodes.rationale: Inspection is read-only; if a query changes state it belongs in drive UI and must represent a real user action.

nodes.label: Recording Capability
nodes.rationale: The recording must show the discriminating final state, not only setup or a loading screen.

nodes.label: Screenshot Capability
nodes.rationale: The screenshot must show enough app chrome to prove that the correct app is under test.

nodes.label: Adapter Setup Check
nodes.rationale: Enable repro work only when all nine steps succeed and no source-channel Slack post is involved.

nodes.label: Control-Adapter Contract
nodes.rationale: Benny does not know how to start or drive every app; the user must configure one control skill or adapter that implements this contract for the target app.

nodes.label: RMChooseToAbort
nodes.rationale: Changes only one of r1 and r2 at a time, so the chart does not draw the steps that stay in one chart state.

nodes.label: RMPrepare
nodes.rationale: Changes only one of r1 and r2 at a time, so the chart does not draw the steps that stay in one chart state.

nodes.label: RMRcvAbortMsg
nodes.rationale: Changes only one of r1 and r2 at a time, so the chart does not draw the steps that stay in one chart state.

nodes.label: RMRcvCommitMsg
nodes.rationale: Changes only one of r1 and r2 at a time, so the chart does not draw the steps that stay in one chart state.

nodes.label: RMPrepare
nodes.rationale: Changes only one of r1 and r2 at a time, so the chart does not draw the steps that stay in one chart state.

nodes.label: Cursor-only features
nodes.rationale: Claude Code has no Cursor Automations, Bugbot, Cursor cloud agents, or built-in PR tool; when a step needs one, emit one 'Skipped in Claude Code' line and continue rather than stopping, asking, or retrying.

nodes.label: Model mapping
nodes.rationale: The model field takes only opus, sonnet, haiku, fable, so Cursor slugs are split into model and effort and the -fast suffix is dropped; non-Claude slugs are omitted so the agent runs on the session model.

nodes.label: Path mapping
nodes.rationale: Claude Code never reads .mdc files, so always-applied rules move to CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md, with the model rule as the exception; the plugin ships the skills, docs/guide/ and README.md, so read the local copy and never fetch it.

nodes.label: Subagent field mapping
nodes.rationale: Subagents run in the background by default and notify on completion, so run_in_background is omitted; readonly agents keep Bash, so the brief must also say 'do not edit files' and git status is checked afterward.

nodes.label: Cursor-to-Claude-Code tool mapping
nodes.rationale: The Skill tool refuses most pstack skills, so running another pstack skill means reading its SKILL.md and following it; AskUserQuestion is absent in -p mode, so ask in plain text.

nodes.label: pstack in Claude Code
nodes.rationale: pstack skills use Cursor names, so this file is read once per session and each Cursor name is mapped with the tables below; if a Cursor field has no row, drop it and say so, and never pass a field or value the tool schema rejects.

nodes.label: pstack:poteto-agent subagent
nodes.rationale: Its model line holds a Cursor slug, so model and effort are passed on every Agent call that spawns it, mapped with the Models table, so that slug never reaches the API.

nodes.label: pstack-models rule (~/.claude/rules/pstack-models.md)
nodes.rationale: Claude Code loads it into every new session, so its role lines are already in context; if they are not, read the file, and if the file or the role's line is missing, use the skill's default slug.

nodes.label: setup-pstack
nodes.rationale: Claude Code loads every .md file in ~/.claude/rules/ into each new session, so setup-pstack writes its rule there instead of CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md.

nodes.label: npx e2e run
nodes.rationale: The final confirmation step after a session-based fix; also the only way to run tests a session cannot run alone.

nodes.label: Attached Session
nodes.rationale: An attached session has the same tools as a normal session on that target, letting an agent inspect a paused test run.

nodes.label: Mobile Device Target
nodes.rationale: On mobile a session and a run on one device fight over it, so close the session before each run unless the target's device is unused by runs.

nodes.label: Parallel Agents (Subagents)
nodes.rationale: Subagents share one server, so each opens its own session and passes its session id to every tools, call, and close_session.

nodes.label: Session
nodes.rationale: A session is for looking and trying; nothing it does is recorded as a test, and only a test it runs reads or writes the replay cache.

nodes.label: SESSION_TEST_UNSUPPORTED
nodes.rationale: A test in a serial group, a test that starts from a setup test's session, and a test that runs as several agents can't run alone in a session; fix those with e2e run.

nodes.label: close_session
nodes.rationale: afterEach hooks and fixture teardown wait for close_session; it also saves any recording still running.

nodes.label: e2e Plugin for Codex and Cursor
nodes.norm_label: e2e plugin for codex and cursor
nodes.rationale: Registers the MCP server as npx -y e2e@<version> mcp, pinned to the plugin's release.

nodes.label: e2e init Command
nodes.rationale: Reuse an existing registration; when adding one, use the project's config so it starts in the project it drives.

nodes.label: e2e MCP Server
nodes.rationale: Ships with the project's e2e dependency; the Codex/Cursor plugin registers it pinned to the plugin's release so it runs that release even when the project has another e2e version.

nodes.label: Content-Driven Breakpoints
nodes.rationale: Don't chase device sizes; let content tell you where to break.

nodes.label: Custom Controls Testing
nodes.rationale: A before/after slider can pass width checks and still refuse to drag on iOS; gestures need real testing.

nodes.label: Input Method Detection
nodes.rationale: Screen size doesn't tell you input method; a laptop can have a touchscreen and a tablet a keyboard.

nodes.label: Mobile-First Design
nodes.rationale: Desktop-first (max-width) means mobile loads unnecessary styles first.

nodes.label: Responsive Images
nodes.rationale: Browser picks the best file based on viewport width and device pixel ratio.

nodes.label: Safe Areas
nodes.rationale: Modern phones have notches, rounded corners, and home indicators that require safe area insets.

nodes.label: Touch Targets
nodes.rationale: Touch users can't hover; targets need 44x44px minimum.

nodes.label: Craft Floor
nodes.rationale: A live session shipped five invented kickers and the documenter wrote their style into DESIGN.md; that is how one violation becomes the house style. A craft-floor refusal must never be canonized into the system.

nodes.label: Direction Contract (THESIS, OWN-WORLD, STORY, FIRST VIEWPORT, FORM)
nodes.norm_label: direction contract (thesis, own-world, story, first viewport, form)
nodes.rationale: The OWN-WORLD block names the world; the build shows how it landed. Where they diverge, the build wins and the prose may note the divergence.

nodes.label: Not-Canonized Defect Line
nodes.rationale: An element the floor bans is recorded as a defect the build carries, never as a design-system rule for future surfaces to inherit.

nodes.label: Impeccable Documenter
nodes.rationale: Ground truth is the shipped artifact: every token and rule must be evidenced by the built code, never by what was planned. Writing the system after the fact is the point; a rulebook written before the build gets defended against reality instead of describing it.

nodes.label: reference/document.md
nodes.rationale: It is the operating spec for DESIGN.md's format, token schema, sidecar, and section order; follow it exactly.

nodes.label: Default Mode
nodes.rationale: Right for ~90% of sessions: a wrong default costs three on-brand variants with similar feel (recoverable), while a wrong departure costs three off-brand variants (unrecoverable).

nodes.label: Departure Mode
nodes.rationale: Triggered only by explicit user redesign intent; a stale critique or old note is not authorization.

nodes.label: Identity Lock (Phase A)
nodes.rationale: Live runs on an existing surface, so the job is variation within identity; the identity sentence keeps every variant reading as the same brand side by side.

nodes.label: Feature-map example
nodes.rationale: Keep the map at the user point of view; discover internals and current code paths at runtime instead of freezing them here. Copy the file outside the pack so pack refreshes do not overwrite it.

nodes.label: Triage label set (bug, enhancement, needs-triage, needs-info, ready-for-agent, ready-for-human, wontfix)
nodes.norm_label: triage label set (bug, enhancement, needs-triage, needs-info, ready-for-agent, ready-for-human, wontfix)

nodes.label: Adapted JUL-122 runner
nodes.rationale: Pending implementation and verification; its complete test suite must pass on Todd's Windows laptop before it is used for delivery.

nodes.label: Mastra Factory (retired)
nodes.rationale: Its server, public endpoint, credentials, database, timers and repository source have been removed; existing Git history and decision records remain only for audit and reference.

nodes.label: Measure the baseline
nodes.rationale: If the symptom does not appear twice on the baseline, there is no baseline. Do not claim that the fix works.

nodes.label: Measure the patched build
nodes.rationale: Do not stop at compilation or tests. The after result must come from a running patched app.

nodes.label: Cleanup
nodes.rationale: Always call the control adapter's cleanup capability; keep artifacts only as long as the configured retention policy allows.

nodes.label: Verify an existing fix mode
nodes.rationale: The existing artifact owns the fix; verify it without editing or authoring a competing patch.

nodes.label: machine/budget (old controller)
nodes.rationale: Deleted in favour of the stock Mastra guard.

nodes.label: scripts/linear-cli.mjs
nodes.rationale: Read-only or comment-only command work may use it; it does not create cards, edit descriptions or change status, and the Linear credential must never leave that subprocess.

nodes.label: Linear
nodes.rationale: Linear holds cards and requirements; GitHub holds code.

nodes.label: Mastra Factory and Intake route (retired)
nodes.rationale: Retired and must not be recreated or used.

nodes.label: Text and attribute matchers
nodes.rationale: Only toHaveText, toContainText, toHaveAccessibleName, toHaveAttribute(name, value) and expect(browser).toHaveURL accept options; any other option such as indeterminate or useInnerText is INVALID_ARGUMENT, in JavaScript too.

nodes.label: Foldables & Orientation
nodes.rationale: Test folded, unfolded, and tabletop postures.

nodes.label: Platform Idiom Translation
nodes.rationale: Translate idioms; never transplant them.

nodes.label: Size Classes / Window Size Classes
nodes.rationale: Drive structure from size classes, never device-model checks.

nodes.label: Phone to Tablet Adaptation
nodes.rationale: A scaled-up phone UI on a tablet is the failure mode.

nodes.label: Web to Native Porting
nodes.rationale: Reconform, don't reflow.

nodes.label: Source-Preview Targets
nodes.rationale: Wrapper and variants must be written in ONE edit; a separate scaffold write reloads the framework before the variant write lands and strands the browser at 0/N.

nodes.label: Svelte Component Preview
nodes.rationale: The browser mounts compiled components so Svelte HMR does not reset page state.

nodes.label: Context-aware menu
nodes.rationale: Never auto-run a command; the recommendation is a suggestion the user confirms.

nodes.label: Webhook Sender Key
nodes.rationale: Keep the sender key on the server; do not put it in the browser, in chat, or in this skill.

nodes.label: Lead agent
nodes.rationale: Reads its model from ~/.config/julia/lead-model at each model call, independently of the coder's pstack role, so an edit reaches the next call with Studio left running.

nodes.label: /architect skill
nodes.rationale: Offers an alternative to taking the first design, so the user picks from evidence.

nodes.label: /how skill
nodes.rationale: Mechanics first, history second: /how explains how a subsystem works before /why explains why it broke.

nodes.label: why Skill
nodes.rationale: Seeds candidate hypotheses with regression history.

nodes.label: Setup pstack Skill
nodes.rationale: Fable and Opus are one vendor, so the Fable entry could judge only where the Opus entry also could.

nodes.label: Maintain Formal Verification Skill
nodes.rationale: A formal check proves a property of what it describes; when the code changes and the verification does not, the check can keep passing while describing code that no longer exists, and that pass looks like a proof.

nodes.label: Confirm and stop
nodes.rationale: Shape never writes code or a direction contract; when no human or structured answer mechanism exists, assumptions are marked plainly and the brief is returned.

nodes.label: Design brief
nodes.rationale: Write the smallest useful brief; use three to five bullets when the task is settled and the full structure only for ambiguous, multi-screen, or standalone planning.

nodes.label: Resolve the design direction
nodes.rationale: New-work owns visual-world and concept choices; discovery is reused and the process returns before contract, persistence, or implementation.

nodes.label: Discovery interview
nodes.rationale: No code or visual direction is chosen during discovery; questions are asked in small rounds and the agent waits for answers.

nodes.label: Round 1: purpose, people, and outcome
nodes.rationale: Ask the two or three questions that most change the result.

nodes.label: Round 2: material, behavior, and boundaries
nodes.rationale: Run only for material unresolved decisions.

nodes.label: Shape (design brief skill)
nodes.rationale: Discover what should be made and how it should work, then return a confirmed design brief without code.

nodes.label: Agent Client Protocol executor
nodes.rationale: A coding agent the user already signs in to runs agent steps over the Agent Client Protocol; no model provider is needed.

nodes.label: context
nodes.rationale: context is what the app calls things, sent to every model call, judges included.

nodes.label: decisionExecutor
nodes.rationale: Decision models pick actions from choices the executor builds; the text model writes field values and upload paths.

nodes.label: executor
nodes.rationale: An executor entry is a custom brain; none inherits model or context from default.

nodes.label: model
nodes.rationale: model drives agent.act; judgments use judge when set, else model.

nodes.label: system prompt
nodes.rationale: system is how the acting agent works, read only by the act loop.

nodes.label: Steering by principle name
nodes.rationale: Each name points at a complete rule the agent has already read, so one phrase redirects work more precisely than a paragraph of instructions; a citation with no decision behind it means the rule was named but not applied.

nodes.label: Enforcement escalation ladder
nodes.rationale: Ranked by how well each option holds: make the mistake impossible with architecture, block it with types or a lint/CI check, catch it with a test, and only then write it down as a doc or agent rule — nothing fails when an agent skips a rule, so documentation comes last. Human review is deliberately not on the list, because a reviewer who must catch the same mistake on every PR is the problem this fixes.

nodes.label: Observer effect in skill evals
nodes.rationale: An agent that knows it is being evaluated behaves differently, so candidates get an organic-looking task in sanitized directories, never the words 'eval' or 'candidate', and never each other's existence.

nodes.label: architect skill
nodes.rationale: Jumping straight to code would lock in the wrong shape; sketch two shapes and pick the one where each piece of state has one owner, each task has one way to do it, and callers need to know least.

nodes.label: correct skill
nodes.rationale: Assume every contributor is an agent that sees only the files it opened, copies the nearest example, and takes the shortest path that compiles; design the repo so a change that looks right from one file is right for the whole repo, fixing each mistake class at the highest level that works (architecture, then types, then lint, then test, docs last).

nodes.label: Authoring or modifying a skill playbook
nodes.norm_label: authoring or modifying a skill playbook

nodes.label: Migrate Callers Then Delete Legacy APIs
nodes.norm_label: migrate callers then delete legacy apis

nodes.label: Tighten
nodes.rationale: Seven ordered steps that push rules up the pyramid (code, then lint/test/CI, then prose) so a plan, brief, card, or prompt is verifiable and ready to hand over unchanged.

nodes.label: tests/run-view.e2e.ts
nodes.rationale: Must run with a single worker because the flow fixture writes to a shared test-results directory.

nodes.label: dashboard/tests/start-server.mjs
nodes.rationale: Pins TZ=UTC and RUN_VIEW_NOW so durations and reset dates are deterministic.

nodes.label: Mastra TokenCostControl
nodes.rationale: Set to $4, scoped to the card (scope: 'resource' with mastra__resourceId set to the card); before each model step it asks Mastra's saved metrics what the card has cost so far and stops the agent with a tripwire at $4 or more.

nodes.label: Helper agents
nodes.rationale: Helper runs the Lead starts share the run's trace, so the guard counts them; a helper may take up to 100 steps.

nodes.label: known limit test
nodes.rationale: Shows 8 loop steps of $3 each, $24 in all, with no stop, because the guard cannot see a run's cost until the run ends.

nodes.label: The Lead agent
nodes.rationale: The Lead's own loop is the exposure, because the guard sees it only when it ends; it may take up to 400 steps.

nodes.label: Arabic-Script Specifics
nodes.rationale: A filter or sanitizer that strips ZWNJ changes meaning; rejecting one Yeh/Kaf variant locks out users whose keyboard sends the other.

nodes.label: impeccable live-complete
nodes.rationale: The command is a gate, not a formality: it refuses with source_dirty while any live-mode leftover remains.

nodes.label: Carbonize Cleanup
nodes.rationale: The carbonize stitch-in is temporary; without rewriting it into permanent form, dead @scope rules, wrapper divs and marker comments accumulate across sessions.

nodes.label: Variant Parameters (Knobs)
nodes.rationale: Coarse knobs drive a CSS variable or data attribute the scoped CSS is authored against, so the browser docks one control per parameter with zero regeneration cost.

nodes.label: Authoring or Modifying a Skill Playbook
nodes.norm_label: authoring or modifying a skill playbook
nodes.rationale: When in doubt, delete: keep only prose that changes a decision, tell it to do the thing and skip the reason, explain only when the rule is confusing without one.

nodes.label: Encode Lessons in Structure
nodes.rationale: Encode a repeated instruction as a lint, metadata flag, runtime check or script instead of more text.

nodes.label: card-path workflow
nodes.rationale: The run form asks for card and kind and nothing else, and the saved state starts empty, so a run started in Studio needs no preparation.

nodes.label: Principle: Subtract Before You Add
nodes.rationale: Removing complexity first gives a simpler base to build on; simplification is a continual investment.

nodes.label: Codex session session-7554.scope
nodes.rationale: Runtime MemoryMax settings (5 GiB for the session, 2 GiB for Studio) do not persist across a reboot or cover a new session.

nodes.label: JUL-361 experiment
nodes.rationale: Each experiment ran in its own systemd user unit with a memory limit so an OOM kill stays contained to that unit.

nodes.label: systemd user unit with memory limit
