nodes.norm_label: systemd user unit with memory limit

nodes.label: JUL-361 memory and crash fix report
nodes.norm_label: jul-361 memory and crash fix report
nodes.rationale: Records the commands' results and limitations; the limits do not prove that concurrent workloads fit on the server or that an install dies before Studio.

nodes.label: Dish
nodes.rationale: A recipe appears at most once per menu.

nodes.label: Ingredient line
nodes.rationale: The written line is the truth; the parsed parts are the understanding.

nodes.label: Menu
nodes.rationale: Past menus move to a Past list by themselves.

nodes.label: Recipe
nodes.rationale: Stored as written; everything else (total time, conversions, scaling, badges, nutrition) is derived on display.

nodes.label: Shared page
nodes.rationale: The only thing in Julia the outside world can see; book recipes never appear on one in full.

nodes.label: Custom Mode
nodes.rationale: A Custom Mode stays in context every turn until exited and stays out of casual turns, unlike a skill attached to one message with Enter.

nodes.label: Playbook
nodes.rationale: Playbooks are step lists inside /poteto-mode rather than skills, so they have no slash command.

nodes.label: Principle
nodes.rationale: One-rule skills that /poteto-mode reads and cites; users steer with the names rather than invoking them.

nodes.label: pstack models rule file
nodes.rationale: Its absence means /setup-pstack has not run, so every role falls back to its default model; the rule applies to new chats only.

nodes.label: /create-formal-verification-skill
nodes.rationale: Without one, no property is checked past what tests reach, so races and invariants go unproven.

nodes.label: /figure-it-out
nodes.rationale: Designs one rigorous run, as opposed to the Autonomous run playbook which drives one task to a finish condition.

nodes.label: /no-comments
nodes.rationale: Strips comments before review using a reviewer that did not write them.

nodes.label: /create-verification-skill
nodes.rationale: Without a verify-* skill agents have no scripted way to drive the app and prove a change works.

nodes.label: Multi-phase plan playbook
nodes.rationale: Writes the plan and does not implement it, for work spanning phases or stacked PRs.

nodes.label: /poteto-mode
nodes.rationale: Matches the task to a playbook, copies the playbook's steps into the todo list, and runs other skills as steps need them; a hand-written skill sequence tends to drop or reorder steps a playbook would keep.

nodes.label: Poteto Help
nodes.rationale: A help question should not start the work: a pstack run spends real tokens, so the user is handed a prompt to send themselves.

nodes.label: /setup-pstack
nodes.rationale: Asks for a reasoning budget, maps a model to each role, and writes a rule; it is the only skill that loads from the user's words.

nodes.label: /sharpen
nodes.rationale: Rewrites a prompt deeper rather than bigger and returns the prompt without doing the task.

nodes.label: Claude Code adapter
nodes.rationale: Maps the Cursor command names to the pstack: prefix and skips steps that need Cursor-only features.

nodes.label: Qualify the artifact
nodes.rationale: A thread claim, tracker status, branch name, or cause hypothesis without a pull request or commit is not enough.

nodes.label: defineTool
nodes.rationale: Project tools use their toModelOutput renderer for strings as well as structured results; error-text and error-json outputs set isError: true.

nodes.label: Carbonize (accept cleanup)
nodes.rationale: On accept the variant's rules move into the stylesheet that already owns the element with real selectors, knob values are baked in, the element is unwrapped and every data-impeccable-* attribute and impeccable-carbonize marker is dropped.

nodes.label: Live Mode
nodes.rationale: Live mode's browser overlay has no native equivalent, so generate is web only; on ios/android/adaptive projects the command is declined in favour of bolder or quieter on the source.

nodes.label: Browser Overlay
nodes.rationale: The overlay preview is the review channel until accept; the page is never screenshotted.

nodes.label: Variants
nodes.rationale: Each variant is a complete replacement of the element; every variant mounts a copy of the element, so an id repeats in the DOM and a unique class is preferred as selector.

nodes.label: Harness Section
nodes.rationale: pstack was written for Cursor, so Cursor-specific instructions are read through harness mappings elsewhere.

nodes.label: /setup-pstack Command
nodes.rationale: The settings file's per-role lines override the defaults and the routed skills' role models.

nodes.label: Show Me Your Work Skill
nodes.rationale: Log is a working artifact by default; commit it only when the work is ambitious enough that a reviewer needs the trail to trust the result.

nodes.label: Device
nodes.rationale: Screen preferences and the current cook-mode step belong to the device, not to a person.

nodes.label: Prep list
nodes.rationale: Regenerating keeps Todd's changes.

nodes.label: createToolLoopExecutor
nodes.rationale: Keeps the loop and replaces prompt and tool vocabulary.

nodes.label: toHaveScreenshot matcher
nodes.rationale: The first run writes the snapshot file and fails: look at it, commit it, rerun.

nodes.label: mask option
nodes.rationale: Locators painted over, for clocks and other changing content.

nodes.label: Screenshot snapshot files
nodes.rationale: Files are per target and OS (-web-linux.png): screenshots written on a Mac never serve Linux CI, so CI's must be written from a CI job with -u.

nodes.label: --update-snapshots (-u)
nodes.rationale: Writes missing and different files and passes, used after an intended UI change.

nodes.label: Craft (deprecated alias)
nodes.rationale: Deprecated alias for an ordinary request to make new visual work; adds no setup, interview, checkpoint, tool, or quality behavior.

nodes.label: Server-Side Validation
nodes.rationale: Never trust client-side only; validate and sanitize all inputs.

nodes.label: poteto-agent Subagent Type
nodes.rationale: poteto-agent defaults to Opus 5.5, so a role set to inherit-parent or auto must spawn a general-purpose subagent instead.

nodes.label: Principle: Foundational Thinking
nodes.rationale: Getting the data structures right makes downstream code obvious; scaffold work that helps every later phase goes first.

nodes.label: Principle: Make Operations Idempotent
nodes.rationale: Deriving each step from existing state rather than from what the previous run intended makes reruns and crash recovery converge to the correct end state.

nodes.label: Principle: Model the Domain
nodes.rationale: The right structure makes invalid states unrepresentable and deletes branches; an abstraction that adds indirection without removing branches or invalid states should be distrusted.

nodes.label: Principle: Separate Before Serializing Shared State
nodes.norm_label: principle: separate before serializing shared state
nodes.rationale: Instructions are not concurrency control, and 'we need a lock' is a smell to check first; two workers writing their own field into one state.json is still shared mutation.

nodes.label: Principle: Migrate Callers Then Delete Legacy APIs
nodes.norm_label: principle: migrate callers then delete legacy apis
nodes.rationale: Preserving compatibility layers leaves long-lived debt; migrating callers and deleting the old API in the same wave avoids it.

nodes.label: Principle: Never Block on the Human
nodes.norm_label: principle: never block on the human
nodes.rationale: Code changes are reversible and reviewable, so a wrong decision usually costs less than blocking; the human supervises asynchronously.

nodes.label: Principle: Outcome-Oriented Execution
nodes.rationale: Keeping every intermediate step fully stable often creates temporary compatibility code that becomes long-lived debt.

nodes.label: Principle: Redesign From First Principles
nodes.rationale: This is the method for preserving option value when integrating changes into an existing design.

nodes.label: Hold
nodes.rationale: Has no [], <>, or ~>, so TLC checks it only in initial states; it must be listed as an INVARIANT to be checked in every state.

nodes.label: Shade
nodes.rationale: Has no [], <>, or ~>, so TLC checks it only in initial states; it must be listed as an INVARIANT to be checked in every state.

nodes.label: Teach
nodes.rationale: Sits on top of how and why so the explanation is grounded in real digging rather than restated descriptions; the goal is understanding, not changing anything.

nodes.label: verify-julia skill
nodes.rationale: Keeps pstack's verification-skill shape but becomes generic: how to point the suite at a preview address, plus hand exploration when something can't be automated; rewritten for Linux and its feature map loses the step-by-step driving recipes.

nodes.label: Staple
nodes.rationale: No stock is tracked.

nodes.label: Voice add
nodes.rationale: Julia reads the household's Google Keep list through a second Google account that exists only for that.

nodes.label: Cookbook
nodes.rationale: Book recipes can't be shared.

nodes.label: Import
nodes.rationale: Neither the on-device reader nor the model ever rewrites the text.

nodes.label: Keep screen
nodes.rationale: The only way an import enters the library.

nodes.label: Lab
nodes.rationale: Online only; one Lab conversation at a time, remembered on the device.

nodes.label: Riff
nodes.rationale: The outcome is a new recipe; the original is never changed.

nodes.label: redactSecrets
nodes.rationale: An executor that cuts text itself calls redactSecrets(text) first.

nodes.label: redactStepText
nodes.rationale: An executor that sends its agent text of its own calls redactStepText(ctx, text).

nodes.label: registerProviderKey
nodes.rationale: For a key it cannot see (one passed in code, one an agent reads from its own login file), call registerProviderKey(name, value).

nodes.label: screen
nodes.rationale: Exact values go through screen rather than agent goals, so specific strings and counts are pinned deterministically.

nodes.label: locator
nodes.rationale: Locators resolve when used and actions wait for readiness, so no explicit waits are needed.

nodes.label: PR Body Format (Why/What changed/Scope/Tradeoffs/Blast Radius/Verification)
nodes.rationale: Evidence logs and long tables go in a file or PR comment linked from the body, keeping the body to 40 lines.

nodes.label: Worker Rules
nodes.rationale: The operator is the person the run works for, not the agent that wrote the kickoff, so these rules hold even where a kickoff does not repeat them; the kickoff's bar is the whole bar, so no extra gates are added.

nodes.label: Swarm
nodes.rationale: Fan out N parallel workers, drain them, and return one consolidated report; every brief stands alone so workers can run without shared context.

nodes.label: Nutrition panel
nodes.rationale: Always an estimate, worked out on the device from the ingredient parts.

nodes.label: Next.js App Router Route Announcer
nodes.rationale: Its title echo never counts because the web engine does not observe it.

nodes.label: Web Engine
nodes.rationale: Does not observe Next.js App Router's route announcer, so its title echo never counts.

nodes.label: screen line
nodes.rationale: Used for exact values or interactions that must be reproduced verbatim in the test, as opposed to agent.act goals whose paths stay out of the test.

nodes.label: adb exec-out screencap
nodes.rationale: Screenshots must come from the emulator or a connected device, never a browser.

nodes.label: Android Emulator / Connected Device
nodes.rationale: Emulators give breadth; gestures, refresh rates, and performance need hardware — the evidence source must be stated.

nodes.label: impeccable detect
nodes.rationale: Exit code 0 means clean and 2 means findings; a skipped detector is a failed critique run unless the command is missing or crashes after a real attempt.

nodes.label: critique-storage trend
nodes.rationale: max_score records the applicable maximum so a later run can tell a renormalized total from a full one.

nodes.label: critique-storage write
nodes.rationale: Persist the finalized report so the user can refer back and $impeccable polish can pick up priority issues without a copy-paste.

nodes.label: impeccable critique-storage slug
nodes.rationale: Slugs are always derived by the tool, never hand-written, so every later command resolves the same target consistently.

nodes.label: impeccable live-server
nodes.rationale: Stopped with --keep-inject because the overlay went in through the browser, so the project's HTML has no script tag to strip; a bare stop would edit the entry file, which a read-only critique should not do.

nodes.label: Assessment A: Design Review
nodes.rationale: Must finish before detector findings enter the parent synthesis context, because detector output is deterministic but still anchors judgment.

nodes.label: Assessment B: Detector + Browser Evidence
nodes.rationale: Mandatory on web and kept isolated from Assessment A until both complete so the LLM review stays unanchored.

nodes.label: Browser Visualization and Overlay Injection
nodes.rationale: A user-visible overlay may only be claimed when script injection succeeded and the detector ran in the page.

nodes.label: Codex Sub-agent Gate
nodes.rationale: Codex's permission model requires asking before spawning, so asking is the normal path rather than a degradation.

nodes.label: Degraded Run Banner
nodes.rationale: A silent degraded critique is a failed critique, so the first line must declare the degradation.

nodes.label: Design Health Score
nodes.rationale: The total is renormalized to the applicable maximum so the rating band stays proportional when heuristics are n/a.

nodes.label: Design Specificity Verdict
nodes.rationale: Placed first in the report because the question is whether the result feels authored for this product or is category-interchangeable.

nodes.label: Desktop App Assessment
nodes.rationale: The app has a single window, so assessments take turns in it rather than running in parallel tabs.

nodes.label: $impeccable critique
nodes.rationale: Persistence is fire-and-forget; failures should not block the rest of the flow.

nodes.label: Native Platform Mode
nodes.rationale: The detector and browser overlay read only web markup, so with no Assessment B there is nothing to isolate Assessment A from and no degraded banner applies.

nodes.label: Snapshot Persistence and Trend
nodes.rationale: Persistence is bookkeeping after delivery, not the end of the run; a report that exists only in the critique store produced nothing.

nodes.label: Targeted Question Close
nodes.rationale: Prose emitted after a structured question is withheld until the user answers, so a report written after the question reads as if the critique never ran.

nodes.label: Report Header Provenance
nodes.rationale: Declaring the method on the first line ensures a degraded run is never silent.

nodes.label: Run Notes
nodes.rationale: Excluded from the persisted snapshot because persistence, trend read, and temp cleanup happen after the snapshot write and would archive stale status.

nodes.label: Sub-agent Gate
nodes.rationale: Two isolated sub-agents are mandatory whenever a Task tool exists; inline execution is a degraded run, not a faster option.

nodes.label: Target Resolution and Slugging
nodes.rationale: Prefer a source path over a dev-server URL when both identify the same surface: ports drift, paths do not. Slugs are never hand-written.

nodes.label: Working Memory Rule
nodes.rationale: Humans can hold ≤4 items in working memory at once (Miller's Law revised by Cowan, 2001).

nodes.label: Critique Reference
nodes.rationale: The chat response is the primary deliverable; the persisted snapshot is only an archive of that run.

nodes.label: .impeccable/critique/ignore.md
nodes.rationale: It is the only prior-run input critique consumes; matching findings are dropped silently.

nodes.label: Predictive Back Gesture
nodes.rationale: System Back must always work; never trap the user or hijack the gesture.

nodes.label: Window Insets / Edge-to-Edge
nodes.rationale: Status bar, navigation bar, display cutout, and IME insets must be applied so content never hides behind system bars or the keyboard.

nodes.label: Bugbot Triage Reference
nodes.rationale: The goal is not to ignore Bugbot by default but to stop treating every comment as a required code change; skipping a noisy code-quality comment is cheap, skipping a real data or security bug is not, so ask when in doubt.

nodes.label: Principle: Attack the Premise
nodes.rationale: When two or more fixes sharing one premise have failed the same gate, the premise is the likelier fault than the fixes; testing it before writing another fix avoids stacking fixes on a false assumption.

nodes.label: Principle: Fix Root Causes
nodes.rationale: A guard is a fix only when the state it handles is legitimate; otherwise the check hides the bug that produced the state.

nodes.label: Principle: Experience First
nodes.rationale: Foundational thinking governs the sequence of work; this principle governs the target. Foundations should serve the experience.

nodes.label: julia-server-tests.timer
nodes.rationale: The timer stays off; the worker was run once by hand with its service PATH.

nodes.label: Backup
nodes.rationale: Refreshed overnight on days something changed; only changed files are touched.

nodes.label: Real Julia
nodes.rationale: Only accepted changes reach it.

nodes.label: Library
nodes.rationale: There is no other grouping: no folders, tags, or categories.

nodes.label: Claude Code Plugin
nodes.rationale: Does not register the MCP server.

nodes.label: afterEach
nodes.rationale: Runs after failures too, with its own cleanup budget.

nodes.label: Assert model-produced facts with toContain
nodes.rationale: Assert the fact a model produced with toContain, not its exact sentence.

nodes.label: beforeAll
nodes.rationale: Per suite realm, worker fixtures only (device, app, screen on mobile).

nodes.label: No sleeps, fixed delays, or polling loops
nodes.norm_label: no sleeps, fixed delays, or polling loops
nodes.rationale: Wait for the state, not a duration: agent.waitFor with a timeout long enough for the slowest case, or a matcher with a longer timeout when a locator names the state exactly.

nodes.label: Run-unique test data
nodes.rationale: Test data gets a run-unique name and afterEach cleanup, so replays and retries never trip over leftovers.

nodes.label: impeccable-documenter agent
nodes.rationale: Writes DESIGN.md and .impeccable/design.json; cannot ask and writes nothing over an existing DESIGN.md without the user's choice.

nodes.label: Surface Brief
nodes.rationale: Precedence for generation: DESIGN.md wins on visual decisions, PRODUCT.md wins on durable product and voice decisions, the surface brief wins on this surface's strategy.

nodes.label: Calibration
nodes.rationale: AI-generated interfaces cluster around a few looks regardless of subject; where the brief leaves the aesthetic free, landing in one means the self-check failed.

nodes.label: Canon Card
nodes.rationale: Author canonCard too: the category standard as one honest card, same anatomy; the page keeps it subordinate, and the counterweights still bind you.

nodes.label: Code-led Build
nodes.rationale: No comp of this page and no apology for it; each card's HTML sketch is what the user chooses from, and the picked one is the composition the build matches and the finish review audits.

nodes.label: Color Strategy
nodes.rationale: Pick a color strategy before picking colors; color commits at page scale, fields that own whole regions, not accents scattered over a neutral ground.

nodes.label: Comp-led Build
nodes.rationale: The chosen card's comp is law, generated before building when it does not yet exist, and the finish review audits the build against it; boldest composition on the table, fix rounds expected, and the comp is non-optional.

nodes.label: Comps phase
nodes.rationale: Three compositional comps of the requested surface at its own viewport, each with a prompt sidecar; the chosen one's sidecar gets approved true.

nodes.label: Decision Page
nodes.rationale: Present the decision visually: write an options payload with the assigned direction leading, its raised lines included.

nodes.label: Direction Contract
nodes.rationale: A direction contract is durable route or artifact strategy, so create or update the brief even when no other surface strategy needs persistence.

nodes.label: Established World
nodes.rationale: A missing DESIGN.md does not erase a coherent identity already in code; document that identity instead of inventing a replacement.

nodes.label: Finish Review
nodes.rationale: Unreviewed and undocumented is unfinished; this build ends with the finish review, the verdict, DESIGN.md, and every shipping raster carrying its provenance.

nodes.label: Incomplete Brand
nodes.rationale: Preserve confirmed assets and recognizable traits, then expand the system with the user for this surface.

nodes.label: Mode Rules
nodes.rationale: They govern every direction, card, and comp for this surface, and where they conflict with shared guidance they win.

nodes.label: No Visual Authority
nodes.rationale: Create a new world with the user.

nodes.label: Pick Card
nodes.rationale: Add one card for your own top-ranked grounded candidate when it is not the assigned direction; the strongest grounded direction is often where most runs in this category land, and the user deciding that trade is the point of showing it.

nodes.label: PRESENTATION Block
nodes.rationale: concept-seed closes every roll with this procedure, condensed, as a PRESENTATION block that names the recorded build path.

nodes.label: Redesign
nodes.rationale: Preserve product truth, content, function, constraints, and explicit brand commitments; replace the old visual world rather than polishing it. The old look is evidence of what the subject is, not authority over what it becomes.

nodes.label: Re-roll
nodes.rationale: Re-roll eliminates every direction already shown, grounded and challenger alike; after two consecutive re-rolls, ask what quality is missing.

nodes.label: Standing Exit
nodes.rationale: Every direction round offers one quiet, permanent alternative, the category standard, played straight; it is the user's door, never yours.

nodes.label: Structured Question Tool
nodes.rationale: A harness that cannot hold a blocking --wait takes the structured tool without starting the page and discloses the substitution in the first reply, so the tab is never left unanswered.

nodes.label: DESIGN.md
nodes.rationale: New worlds and approved system changes require a token-bearing DESIGN.md and .impeccable/design.json, not prose alone.

nodes.label: Stable selectors
nodes.rationale: Never use generated CSS or StyleX classes, dynamic hashes, child indexes, or brittle DOM position.

nodes.label: github() reporter
nodes.rationale: On GitHub Actions posts one pull request comment per run (edited on rerun) plus the job summary; needs pull-requests: write and GITHUB_TOKEN or GH_TOKEN.

nodes.label: htmlReporter()
nodes.rationale: One page that opens from disk; media: 'embed' makes one shareable file except downloads the runner could not scan for secrets, media: 'none' leaves media out.

nodes.label: run()
nodes.rationale: Returns the suite report without exiting the caller; a runtime config uses one in-process worker, and overlapping runs reject with RUNNER_BUSY.

nodes.label: Exit codes
nodes.rationale: The highest code present wins (130 > 4 > 3 > 2 > 1 > 0); exit 2 is deterministic and never retried, only exit 3 is worth a job-level retry.

nodes.label: junit.xml
nodes.rationale: For CI summaries; a failure screenshot is linked as a system-out attachment relative to $CI_PROJECT_DIR so GitLab shows it in the test report.

nodes.label: report.json
nodes.rationale: Written for scripts rather than reading; the one record of every result, passing ones included, whatever the reporters.

nodes.label: summary.md
nodes.rationale: Meant to be pasted into a pull request or handoff.

nodes.label: timings.json
nodes.rationale: Records how long each file took; with more than one worker the next run starts the longest known files first, after any with no time.

nodes.label: results/<test>/trace.md
nodes.rationale: Written per failed, timed-out, interrupted or flaky test; read it first.

nodes.label: TDD Bug Fix
nodes.rationale: Make the broken behavior executable before changing production code, but prefer no new test over a bad test when the test path is expensive, brittle, or integration-heavy.

nodes.label: Unknown
nodes.rationale: Settled by research or a prototype before triage.

nodes.label: scripts/worktree-audit.sh
nodes.rationale: Reads paths from `git worktree list` rather than hand-typed paths, since a hand-typed path misses worktrees living under .cursor/worktrees.

nodes.label: /poteto-mode
nodes.rationale: You don't need to name a playbook or list skills; a stated goal plus a checkable outcome ('repro first') is all the routing signal it needs.

nodes.label: principle-encode-lessons-in-structure
nodes.rationale: Its rule is 'the instruction is the symptom'.

nodes.label: The pstack guide
nodes.rationale: pstack works best when you stop micromanaging the agent: describe the goal and how you'll know it's done, and let /poteto-mode pick the playbook and show the evidence.

nodes.label: /poteto-help skill
nodes.rationale: It answers, hands you a prompt to send, and links the skill or guide page the answer came from, but does not start the work, because a pstack run spends real tokens; it runs only when you type it.

nodes.label: Refactoring Playbook
nodes.rationale: You own the contract; the structure changes but the behavior does not. Cleanup that reveals a missing feature or a real bug is split out and the structural change ships first against the pinned contract.

nodes.label: Runtime Forensics Playbook
nodes.rationale: You own the diagnosis: instrument the live process rather than theorizing from source; the deliverable is a cited diagnosis, not a fix.

nodes.label: Session Pickup Playbook
nodes.rationale: The prior trail is authoritative input; resist the bias to re-derive it, and do not redo completed work.

nodes.label: Trace Forensics Playbook
nodes.rationale: The capture already exists and is a fixed dataset: read it, don't re-run it. Without a paired capture the finding is the strongest hypothesis the artifact supports, not a confirmed cause.

nodes.label: Visual Parity Playbook
nodes.rationale: Equivalence is verified by image diff, not by eye; the baseline is the spec and is never touched, and no baseline means no parity claim.

nodes.label: Worktree and Simulator Cleanup Playbook
nodes.rationale: This is the one playbook that deletes user state with no code review to catch a slip, so the audit gates are the review; the pinned and active chats are the real artifact and win over the tool's bucket advice.

nodes.label: Patterns & Systemic Issues
nodes.rationale: Recurring problems indicate systemic gaps rather than one-off mistakes.

nodes.label: Platform Conformance
nodes.rationale: Marked CRITICAL: it determines whether the app reads as a native app or as a ported website.

nodes.label: Platform Conformance Verdict
nodes.rationale: Presented first because the native-vs-ported-website verdict frames every other finding.

nodes.label: Positive Findings
nodes.rationale: Celebrate what works so good practices are maintained and replicated.

nodes.label: P0-P3 Severity Levels
nodes.rationale: Keep P3s few: a long tail of minor issues buries the ones that matter.

nodes.label: Native App Audit Reference
nodes.rationale: A code-level technical audit, not a design critique: issues are documented rather than fixed so that other commands can address them.

nodes.label: Advisor
nodes.rationale: Sees a card only with a PASS and its evidence, after a second FAIL, or when the builder is blocked; checks each PASS for a rubber stamp, which counts as a FAIL.

nodes.label: Agents and runners
nodes.rationale: Agents use judgment and never touch Linear or GitHub; runners are Mastra workflows that start every agent and do the rest by fixed rules, signing what they post.

nodes.label: Dashboard
nodes.rationale: Every piece of work is started and watched from the dashboard, and its proof is something Todd can see working on a screen he uses, without reading code.

nodes.label: Evidence review (superseded by Shipping)
nodes.rationale: The 'is the evidence there' gate was dropped (no evidence index); only 'is the evidence right' was kept, and it was later renamed Shipping.

nodes.label: JUL-252 (evidence review card)
nodes.rationale: Canceled as superseded; the evidence-review instruction agreed on 25 October must not be sent.

nodes.label: JUL-360 (build slice caps)
nodes.rationale: Superseded the earlier no-cap rule: a build slice stops at its caps and exploration gates, enforced as hard ceilings on real calls.

nodes.label: Live check
nodes.rationale: The card moves to Complete only after the live address serves the merged commit and the regression suite passes there; on failure the card stops and Todd is notified, nothing rolls back by itself.

nodes.label: Mastra workflow (the path)
nodes.rationale: A homemade runner script is the wrong shape: PR #387's runner is closed unmerged; Mastra keeps each step's state, the FAIL count and the pause for Todd's yes.

nodes.label: Merge
nodes.rationale: Shipping merges only after Todd's yes and only while its PASS still covers the current code (patch-id rule); changed code goes back through Shipping.

nodes.label: Old machine
nodes.rationale: Removed from main on 26 Oct 2026 and kept at tag old-machine-final, overriding the 25 Oct 'untouched until milestone 1' line.

nodes.label: Planner agent
nodes.rationale: Works with Todd at the Idea step; any frontier paid model can fill it.

nodes.label: PR #387 (homemade runner)
nodes.rationale: Closed unmerged because a homemade runner script is the wrong shape for the path.

nodes.label: Preview
nodes.rationale: Julia cards use the PR's Vercel preview; dashboard and machine cards use a second copy of the dashboard on the server at its own Tailscale port so the live dashboard stays on main.

nodes.label: Remediation
nodes.rationale: A first Shipping FAIL moves the card to Remediation for one round of defect fixing; a second FAIL runs the Investigation playbook for the root cause and the card stops.

nodes.label: Retro
nodes.rationale: A retro PR waits for Todd's approval because it changes the environment every future card runs in, which is where human review has the most leverage (poteto).

nodes.label: Shipping (independent review)
nodes.rationale: Wrong-but-present evidence got past pstack and the builder's report twice on 23 Oct and was stopped only by the advisor's human review, so an independent agent runs the PR the way Todd would and decides PASS or FAIL per criterion.

nodes.label: Start's admission check
nodes.rationale: Refuses a card that doesn't qualify on structure, not prose; removed with the old machine on 26 Oct.

nodes.label: Todd
nodes.rationale: Todd's role: ideas, settling cards, UAT, approving retro lessons.

nodes.label: UAT
nodes.rationale: A card gets UAT only if it changes something Todd uses directly; UAT steps live on the card so the builder and Prove It Works aim at exactly what Todd will try.

nodes.label: Codebase improvements
nodes.rationale: Agents copy what exists and take the shortest path, so make the easy thing the right thing; categorically eliminate problems through code and you won't need to think about it again.

nodes.label: /correct
nodes.rationale: In pstack, /correct is this pyramid as a working procedure.

nodes.label: Human review
nodes.rationale: The hardest to scale; at the rate agents land code it is impossible to thoroughly review every PR, so spend the effort on the highest leverage point.

nodes.label: Prose
nodes.rationale: Comments, rules, AGENTS.md, skills — anything that can't be enforced and requires agent judgment; use it minimally.

nodes.label: Static analysis
nodes.rationale: Lint rules, tests, CI, verification (e.g. TLA+) are very token efficient ways to catch issues ahead of time.

nodes.label: addInitScript
nodes.rationale: Runs before the page's own scripts; call it before app.open.

nodes.label: clearCookies
nodes.rationale: Remove cookies matching every string or RegExp filter; no options removes all cookies, other storage stays.

nodes.label: emulateMedia
nodes.rationale: What the page's @media rules and matchMedia read, for the rest of the test; call it before app.open to load the page with it.

nodes.label: evaluate
nodes.rationale: Runs a function or source string in the page, JSON in and out, no closures.

nodes.label: frameLocator
nodes.rationale: A Screen scoped to one iframe; keeps locator(css) and frameLocator(css) for nesting.

nodes.label: goto
nodes.rationale: Navigation on the test timeout by default; goto takes a base-relative path.

nodes.label: keyboard
nodes.rationale: Unfocused input; only down(key) holds a key or modifier until up(key). Prefer locator.press and locator.fill.

nodes.label: locator
nodes.rationale: Raw CSS or XPath; not portable, a last resort.

nodes.label: onDialog
nodes.rationale: Awaited; resolves to an async unsubscribe. Register it before the tap that opens the dialog.

nodes.label: setCookies
nodes.rationale: A target is an http(s) URL or a domain.

nodes.label: unroute
nodes.rationale: Removes routes registered with the same pattern, method included, rather than URL-matching them.

nodes.label: unrouteAll
nodes.rationale: Removes every route; configured headers stay.

nodes.label: waitForDownload
nodes.rationale: absolutePath names the saved runner-side file for reading its contents, including with a hosted browser.

nodes.label: waitForDownloads
nodes.rationale: Calls the trigger once and returns count of those results in start order.

nodes.label: waitForPopup
nodes.rationale: Makes the tab the trigger opens active and resolves with it.

nodes.label: waitForResponse
nodes.rationale: Resolves once the headers arrive; start the wait before the request, including the first browser.goto or app.open.

nodes.label: waitForURL
nodes.rationale: waitForURL matches like toHaveURL.

nodes.label: APIs live in the same suite
nodes.norm_label: apis live in the same suite
nodes.rationale: Use fetch plus value matchers in a test.extend fixture that reads browser.cookies() when the API needs the session.

nodes.label: Browser Fixture
nodes.rationale: Prefer app and screen; browser is for what only a browser has, and a portable suite declares requires: ['browser'].

nodes.label: Selectors come from the source
nodes.rationale: Add an aria-label or heading where the app has no accessible name rather than fall back to browser.locator('.btn-primary').

nodes.label: Build the Lever
nodes.rationale: The tool is the artifact a reviewer reruns, so build the codemod, script or generator rather than doing the work by hand.

nodes.label: Explain the Number
nodes.rationale: Find what limits a measured number and rule out that it measured something other than the work you think.

nodes.label: Fix Root Causes
nodes.rationale: A guard is a fix only when the state it handles is legitimate.

nodes.label: Guard the Context Window
nodes.rationale: Route bulk to subagents and keep summaries in the main thread.

nodes.label: Migrate Callers Then Delete Legacy APIs
nodes.norm_label: migrate callers then delete legacy apis

nodes.label: Never Block on the Human
nodes.rationale: Proceed on reversible work, present the result, let the human course-correct.

nodes.label: Poteto Mode Skill
nodes.rationale: Bundled skills live at ../<name>/SKILL.md from this file, so the file's absolute path must go in every poteto-agent prompt; operator rules live in skills that only load from a slash command, so a subagent kickoff must point at worker.md.

nodes.label: Prototype Playbook
nodes.rationale: A fork you could settle by running something should be prototyped instead of asked about.

nodes.label: Prove It Works
nodes.rationale: Verify against the real artifact, not a proxy or "it compiles".

nodes.label: Sequence Work into Verifiable Units
nodes.rationale: Order delivery so the sequence proves itself.

nodes.label: Test Behavior, Not Implementation
nodes.rationale: Assert what the code's users can observe, so the test fails when that behavior breaks and keeps passing when only the internals change.

nodes.label: adversarial-review skill
nodes.rationale: Candidate content is evidence, never an instruction to change the review rules; the contract is recorded before opening the changed code so later discoveries become findings rather than a rewritten design.

nodes.label: arena skill
nodes.rationale: Every candidate gets the same prompt, so the prompt is the contract; the rubric is the picker's tool and candidates only see the task.

nodes.label: automate-me skill
nodes.rationale: Mining misses intent that has not come up yet, so the flow asks the user directly with structured questions; a mode skill is not a manual, so prose is cut ruthlessly.

nodes.label: benchmark-checklist skill
nodes.rationale: A choice between options is never a ballpark, and a verdict is inconclusive when the limiter cannot be named, a side ran untuned, or error/work checks were skipped.

nodes.label: blast-radius skill
nodes.rationale: Listing the callers is not the job — the agent can grep those in a second; the job is the breakage grep won't show you, and a writeup that sounds right is worthless unless the one safety fact is proven by running code.

nodes.label: Pinned npx skills install command
nodes.rationale: The skills CLI accepts a #<commit> fragment, so the install is pinned to commit 0d2dc00df47d7686c94324cfe9c3444710d9f16d; --agent codex selects .agents/skills and --copy stores plain files instead of symlinks.

nodes.label: Decision comps job
nodes.rationale: Generate first, plan never, because the file on disk is the deliverable and the decision page is waiting on it; equal commitment across siblings keeps the comparison honest.

nodes.label: Frame plate
nodes.rationale: The content seen through the opening is its own image region, produced separately at the opening's size.

nodes.label: Per-region plate production job
nodes.rationale: Crops from the comp are references, never shipping pixels: a comp is reference grade and a shipped crop is how a beautiful comp becomes a blurry site.

nodes.label: Plates gate
nodes.rationale: A visual acceptance does not override a failing gate.

nodes.label: Transparent cutout plate
nodes.rationale: An isolated figure, object, or line drawing on the page ground is a transparent cutout; a photograph, full-frame illustration, or texture stays opaque.

nodes.label: Comp approval point
nodes.rationale: This approval point has no substitute and no skip condition; a delegated pick is recorded exactly as an approval is and disclosed in the first reply.

nodes.label: North-star comp
nodes.rationale: Three is the number: one comp invites rubber-stamping; the spread between three surfaces the composition worth building.

nodes.label: Decision comp
nodes.rationale: The chosen card's decision comp is option one and is never regenerated; comps two and three vary what the first held fixed, from the direction in words rather than with the first comp as an input image, because a reference image anchors the layout and three comps collapse into one composition.

nodes.label: MODE RULES (COMPS) concept-seed block
nodes.rationale: The MODE RULES block governs the comps together with this file and wins where they conflict.

nodes.label: Phased build (comps, spec, plates phases)
nodes.rationale: A comp rendered before the comps phase is open sits outside the state, and a session resumed from that point has no phases to follow.

nodes.label: Plate (raster region asset)
nodes.rationale: Writing CSS for a sculpted panel's finish, or a many-vertex clip-path for a torn edge, is the quiet deletion of the approved design.

nodes.label: Impeccable Asset Producer (degraded inline role)
nodes.rationale: This harness has no subagent capability, so the role runs inline: produce the full output contract first, then act on it yourself.

nodes.label: .impeccable/mocks/
nodes.rationale: Comps are saved under .impeccable/mocks/ so they survive the session.

nodes.label: agent.act
nodes.rationale: The agent does the flow; expect pins what must be true at the end, and that check lets the replay cache rerun every goal before it later.

nodes.label: agent fixture
nodes.rationale: Defaults to the run's agent; a configured name (agents.<name>) or a list run once per agent; innermost wins.

nodes.label: agent.waitFor
nodes.rationale: Closes the act block by waiting for the state the action triggers.

nodes.label: test.fail
nodes.rationale: Covers test failures and timeouts only: an infrastructure error such as ENGINE_FAILURE or a blocked agent verdict still fails the test.

nodes.label: test.fixme
nodes.rationale: test.skip's three forms; reported skipped with cause "fixme".

nodes.label: test.for
nodes.rationale: test.each without the spread: (row, { app }).

nodes.label: test.only
nodes.rationale: Local only: CI fails with ONLY_IN_CI.

nodes.label: test.runIf
nodes.rationale: Equivalent to test.skipIf(!condition).

nodes.label: test.setTimeout
nodes.rationale: Body or beforeEach: the attempt's timeout, counted from its start; in beforeAll: that hook's own.

nodes.label: test.skip
nodes.rationale: Throws: the body stops here, reported skipped; call it before the first step.

nodes.label: test.skipIf
nodes.rationale: Condition read at collection: truthy registers it skipped, as { skip: true }.

nodes.label: unique()
nodes.rationale: A fixture's run-unique value in a goal's params must go in as unique(value), or every run misses the cache.

nodes.label: Action Cache
nodes.rationale: The cache keeps entries when a later line fails, so each run pays model calls only for its new part; a retry never replays, and with CI set the cache records nothing by default, so grow the test outside CI.

nodes.label: agent topic
nodes.rationale: A project tool that seeds data (topic agent) gets there in one call while exploring over MCP.

nodes.label: Arrange-act-assert structure
nodes.rationale: Arrange, act, assert in that order with a blank line between the three blocks; no check sits between arrange and act steps, and the arrange block's closing wait keeps the setup goals cached while you fix the act or the assertions.

nodes.label: Grow a Test One Screen at a Time
nodes.norm_label: grow a test one screen at a time
nodes.rationale: Write up to the next unseen screen, end with a temporary check, run it, then replace the check with the next part; the finished test keeps only its outcome checks in the assert block.

nodes.label: One behavior per test
nodes.rationale: When a test fails, its title alone should say what broke, with no debugging needed; an "and" in a title usually means two tests.

nodes.label: Secret Redaction
nodes.rationale: A registered value passed as a plain string is redacted in reports, step labels, the executor and the model, so the agent cannot type it; pass the handle instead.

nodes.label: Approved Comp
nodes.rationale: The comp is the spec for composition, topology, element inventory, density, lettering character, and material; it is not a pixel spec for semantics, accessibility, or responsive reflow.

nodes.label: Check 0: Evidence
nodes.rationale: A viewport nobody captured is a viewport nobody inspected, and it cannot ship; a verdict derived from a broken capture launders the breakage into an approval.

nodes.label: Check 2: Fidelity
nodes.rationale: Imitation material is the single most reliable mark of machine-made design; medium is part of the promise.

nodes.label: Check 6: Floor
nodes.rationale: Fidelity to a comp cannot authorize what the craft floor refuses; hookless harnesses reach the reviewer with no mechanical findings, so a banned element missed here ships.

nodes.label: Disposition
nodes.rationale: The word is derived, never felt; the reviewer is the last gate before the user, not a colleague softening news for a colleague.

nodes.label: Material Fixes
nodes.rationale: Ordered most material first, fidelity failures ahead of craft, at most eight.

nodes.label: Quality Bar Card
nodes.rationale: The card governs commitment and finish, never composition.

nodes.label: Verdict pass
nodes.rationale: A verdict pass scores the listed fixes and nothing else; it cannot support a claim that no material issues remain.

nodes.label: Impeccable Finish Reviewer
nodes.rationale: Fresh eyes on a done artifact, outside the build thread's attention gravity; the reviewer edits nothing and the parent applies fixes.

nodes.label: run.mjs
nodes.rationale: Rounds that already posted are carried forward from record.json so a crash between two reviews cannot post the first determination twice.

nodes.label: workflow.test.mjs
nodes.rationale: Runs on the server; a runner without the Mastra Code program reports those rounds as skipped and names the missing packages.

nodes.label: machine/shipping/determination.mjs
nodes.rationale: Reused rather than copied so a determination looks the same on both machines.

nodes.label: machine/shipping/run-parts.mjs
nodes.rationale: Reused rather than copied so a determination looks the same on both machines.

nodes.label: machine/shipping/workflow.mjs
nodes.rationale: Reused rather than copied so a determination looks the same on both machines; also holds the twenty-minute review clock.

nodes.label: MAX_REVIEWS = 2
nodes.rationale: The review limit is one constant in workflow.mjs so the loop length is defined in a single place.

nodes.label: investigate step
nodes.rationale: Two failures in a row get a root cause instead of a third try.

nodes.label: Mastra workflow `remediation`
nodes.rationale: One straight chain where each step reads the record and returns it unchanged when it does not apply, so a first review that passes walks the chain without waking anybody.

nodes.label: /verify-<app> skill
nodes.rationale: Reproducing on main lets the run stop early when the bug is already gone.

nodes.label: Doctor check
nodes.rationale: `npx e2e list` loads the config and prints every test-target pair without starting anything, so a config error shows here first; an agent runs Doctor first whenever anything looks off.

nodes.label: e2e explore
nodes.rationale: The steps prove the charter ran, not the exit code: `1` is also what a run that executed no step exits with.

nodes.label: e2e skill
nodes.rationale: The e2e skill is the reference for everything e2e does; link to it rather than restate it, and prefer `npx e2e guide <topic>` when the two differ.

nodes.label: Evidence (.e2e/)
nodes.rationale: The next run clears `.e2e/results/`, Doctor included, so a proof that must outlive it runs with `--output .e2e/proof/<name>` or its attempt directory is copied out before anything else runs.

nodes.label: bug bash
nodes.rationale: Parallel explore runs where each bug must be proven by a repro test.

nodes.label: Proof standards
nodes.rationale: The next e2e run clears .e2e/results/, so a proof that must outlive later runs uses --output .e2e/proof/<name>.

nodes.label: Smoke test
nodes.rationale: The whole regression suite reruns on the preview so Todd never sees a broken preview; a failure goes back to the build.

nodes.label: Verify the playground (example skill)
nodes.rationale: This skill only says what is true of this app; the e2e skill is read first for everything e2e does.

nodes.label: impeccable-asset-producer agent
nodes.rationale: Shipped asset producer spawned with the spec path to produce all plates when parallel subagents are available.

nodes.label: impeccable build-phase advance
nodes.rationale: Exit 2 means the gate failed and printed why; fix that and advance again, writing nothing for a later phase while an earlier gate is open.

nodes.label: impeccable build-phase record hero
nodes.rationale: Records the hero capture once so plate regions can be seen reading as match before any text exists.

nodes.label: impeccable build-phase scaffold
nodes.rationale: Writes the measured layout as CSS custom properties and a reference page with every region at its box and every plate placed.

nodes.label: impeccable comp-spec
nodes.rationale: Measures the comp into a spec carrying each region's box, sampled palette, and medium; the printed spec is the build's reference from here on.

nodes.label: impeccable embed-prompt
nodes.rationale: Embeds the exact generation prompt for a produced raster or the origin for a sourced one; the scan only reads and never deletes flagged files.

nodes.label: impeccable font-match
nodes.rationale: Type is measured, not guessed: reads cap height, width class, and weight off the pixels and ranks candidates by fingerprint distance.

nodes.label: impeccable generate-image
nodes.rationale: API fallback for plate generation when the harness-native image tool is unavailable.

nodes.label: Author the assets
nodes.rationale: Gradients, glass, generic icon tiles, and many-vertex clip-path polygons where an authored asset belongs are the gap wearing chrome.

nodes.label: Build-phase state machine
nodes.rationale: Models systematically believe their recreation succeeded when it did not, so the build runs as an on-disk state machine whose gates measure the screen against the comp.

nodes.label: Code-led build path
nodes.rationale: Without a comp, ambition lives in the direction contract's FIRST VIEWPORT block and the named signature interaction, audited in behavior by the finish reviewer.

nodes.label: Comp-led build path
nodes.rationale: An approved comp is a measured spatial contract, not a mood board; only the user can downgrade its authority in explicit words.

nodes.label: First viewport is a thesis
nodes.rationale: If someone left after one viewport, what would they describe an hour later? If the honest answer is a mood, the concept has not committed yet.

nodes.label: Hero phase
nodes.rationale: This is where the run's ambition is won or lost, and a retry here costs minutes where a rebuild verdict at the finish costs the run.

nodes.label: Author motion as material
nodes.rationale: Give the page the form's native motion once, orchestrated, rather than scattered hover effects; bound expensive effects and keep content visible by default.

nodes.label: Motion phase
nodes.rationale: The signature interaction, reveals, and motion, orchestrated once rather than scattered.

nodes.label: Plates phase
nodes.rationale: Every raster region ships as a plate regenerated at asset resolution from its comp crop; a crop of the comp is a reference, never a shipping pixel.

nodes.label: Prove, don't claim
nodes.rationale: Show the subject doing its job with specifics a competitor could not copy-paste; demonstration data is design material and claims stay uninventable.

nodes.label: Raster provenance
nodes.rationale: Every build raster keeps its provenance: the exact generation prompt for a produced raster, the origin for a sourced, stock, or pre-existing one.

nodes.label: Use real, verified imagery
nodes.rationale: Search for the subject's physical object rather than the category; one decisive photo beats five mediocre ones, and stock URLs must resolve.

nodes.label: Pace the scroll like a studio
nodes.norm_label: pace the scroll like a studio
nodes.rationale: Vary density, scale, image, motion, and quiet inside one grammar; a dense passage earns a quiet one, and the page ends anchored by a real close.

nodes.label: Sections phase
nodes.rationale: Build the rest of the surface inside the spec's system; where the comp does not cover a region, it inherits the recorded system.

nodes.label: Spec phase
nodes.rationale: Anything not in the spec does not exist on the page: no borders, rules, containers, or chrome the comp does not show.

nodes.label: Build the form's web leverage
nodes.rationale: When the chosen world names a technique, build the technique itself, not a static imitation of it.

nodes.label: Benny configuration
nodes.rationale: User-owned copies live outside .cursor/automations/benny/ so pack refreshes never touch them; secrets go in a secret manager or environment, never in YAML, prompts, or committed configuration.

nodes.label: Benny control adapter
nodes.rationale: If any capability is missing the repro automation stays disabled: it must fail closed rather than claim a reproduction it did not perform.

nodes.label: Benny feature map
nodes.rationale: Kept at the user point of view and not frozen to implementation details or current code paths, so the map survives code churn.

nodes.label: benny-reproduce automation
nodes.rationale: Waits for a trusted triage marker and must fail closed rather than claim a reproduction it did not perform.

nodes.label: Benny routing map
nodes.rationale: Owner pings stay off by default; a ping is allowed only for a configured feature owner or a confirmed likely regression author, and without a map triage must not guess a destination or owner.

nodes.label: Thread safety test
nodes.rationale: Both automations stay disabled until all seven checks pass, because a root-message leak or a spoofed marker would corrupt the shared thread.

nodes.label: benny-triage automation
nodes.rationale: Replies only inside the triggering thread and never posts a source-channel root message, so report threads stay the single source of truth.

nodes.label: Benny verdict markers
nodes.rationale: A single configured marker per thread-only verdict lets repro accept only trusted triage output.

nodes.label: built-in /automate skill
nodes.rationale: The built-in automate skill is creation-only and is the only finish path for new automations; it must not be used to search for, inspect, or update existing automations.

nodes.label: pstack plugin
nodes.rationale: Enabled through the target repository's project-scoped .cursor/settings.json so a fresh agent rooted in the target repository receives pstack; a skill loaded from the current session or a user-scoped plugin does not count.

nodes.label: tdd Skill
nodes.rationale: Failing-test-first cadence applies only when the bug has a cheap local test path.

nodes.label: Set up Benny
nodes.rationale: Benny ships as a dormant automation pack inside pstack; the plugin manifest exposes only pstack's normal skill root, so this file and the two operational files are not slash skills and must be read directly from the copied pack.

nodes.label: scripts/check-graph-sources.mjs
nodes.rationale: Fails CI if graphify-out/graph.json references any path the repository does not carry.

nodes.label: .graphifyignore
nodes.rationale: Keeps historical records, throwaway fixtures, duplicate skill catalogs, and images out of the graph; .gitignore is read first so .artifacts/, .commandcode/, .mastra/ and node_modules/ are already excluded.

nodes.label: scripts/julia-agents.mjs
nodes.rationale: Supplies the Command Code key so both graphs use the endpoint already configured for the agents, involving no new service; the small chunk budget exists because the model truncates a large chunk and the retry re-sends it.

nodes.label: /home/ubuntu/.config/git/julia-hooks
nodes.rationale: The server sets core.hooksPath outside the repository, so a clone inheriting it needs these chain files because git ignores .git/hooks when that setting is present.

nodes.label: dashboard/config/roles.json
nodes.rationale: Supplies the paid everyday-coding model (feature-refactoring role) used for extraction.

nodes.label: graphify-out/mastra/versions.json
nodes.rationale: Records the installed package versions the Mastra graph was built from.

nodes.label: AGENTS.md
nodes.rationale: Its ## Graphify section tells every coding session when to ask the graph first.

nodes.label: dashboard/scripts/install-service.mjs
nodes.rationale: Refuses to run off this server or from the operator checkout or a lane worktree, and running it twice is safe.

nodes.label: scripts/install-lead-model.mjs
nodes.rationale: Creates the initial lead-model setting once and preserves an existing file.

nodes.label: scripts/server/mastracode-tmpfiles.conf
nodes.rationale: Excludes /tmp/mc from every cleanup rule after a 13 November cleanup aborted every run in progress.

nodes.label: Julia Runner GitHub App
nodes.rationale: A personal token cannot create check runs (POST /check-runs answers 403), so the runner signs an RS256 JWT and trades it for an installation token.

nodes.label: /tmp/mc signal sockets
nodes.rationale: An idle folder is safe but a running session's folder is not, and telling them apart means finding its sockets in use, so no cleanup script of ours may remove it.

nodes.label: browser.waitForURL
nodes.rationale: One of the checks that can confirm a recording.

nodes.label: expect.poll
nodes.rationale: Confirms nothing for cache purposes.

nodes.label: locator.waitFor
nodes.rationale: One of the checks that can confirm a recording.

nodes.label: Replay Verification Check
nodes.rationale: An entry is written only after a later verification passes, so an unchecked act never replays; a plain-value expect, expect.poll, agent.extract, another act, or the attempt passing confirms nothing.

nodes.label: agent.act
nodes.rationale: One goal per act; a split flow fails at the goal that broke, and each goal replays from its own recording and gets its own maxSteps and maxModelCalls.

nodes.label: agent fixture
nodes.rationale: Each call is one bounded invocation: fresh redacted observation, deadline, model-call budget, no shared transcript. No agent step, no model calls.

nodes.label: agent.assert
nodes.rationale: assert does not poll; too little on screen to decide is ASSERTION_INCONCLUSIVE, so reach the right screen first and ask about what is visible.

nodes.label: model call budgets
nodes.rationale: STEP_TIMEOUT and STEP_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED fail the test; smaller goals help.

nodes.label: explore option
nodes.rationale: Helps when a list fits on a tablet but needs scrolling on a phone.

nodes.label: agent.extract
nodes.rationale: The model sees the schema's shape, never its value rules (min, max, lengths, patterns), which check what it read.

nodes.label: observe tool
nodes.rationale: Re-read the screen after waiting on work in progress, or to check whether a press that commits something went through.

nodes.label: onBeforeAction hook
nodes.rationale: Gives a debug view that pairs each action with the screen it started on; runs before replayed actions too.

nodes.label: params option
nodes.rationale: Values go in params, never expanded; a run-unique unique() keeps the cache working across runs.

nodes.label: screenshot tool
nodes.rationale: Attaches viewport pixels; every later result then carries one.

nodes.label: Secret
nodes.rationale: The model sees its name, the runner fills the field.

nodes.label: session
nodes.rationale: For signed-in personas, pair an agent with a session in a describe block repeated per persona.

nodes.label: act tool set
nodes.rationale: The tools, one per engine action; the agent picks the verb and names the target as the screen names it.

nodes.label: type_secret tool
nodes.rationale: Plaintext never reaches the model; an undeclared name fills nothing.

nodes.label: upload tool
nodes.rationale: Outside the project root or hidden (.env) is POLICY_DENIED.

nodes.label: vision option
nodes.rationale: 'only' never falls back to the tree: unprovably masked pixels fail with POLICY_DENIED.

nodes.label: agent.waitFor
nodes.rationale: Never sleep for a fixed time to let the app settle: a sleep is too short on a slow run and wasted time on a fast one; waitFor returns as soon as the state appears.

nodes.label: start_recording
nodes.rationale: Record a demo or a bug for a pull request once the screen is set up; videos are not masked, so secrets must stay off screen.

nodes.label: stop_recording
nodes.rationale: Stop when the part worth watching is over; the video is saved under <output>/videos/<session>/.

nodes.label: Grammar Verbs
nodes.rationale: A verb the engine cannot honor is not listed and fails with UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY.

nodes.label: Session Recording
nodes.rationale: Videos are not masked, so secrets must be kept off screen while recording.

nodes.label: buildPath Config Key
nodes.rationale: An unread value does not fall back to the opposite path, so a project meaning code has been building comp-led.

nodes.label: Deprecated Fields
nodes.rationale: Preserving it just in case is how a retired axis keeps steering current output.

nodes.label: design-md-drift Finding
nodes.rationale: A commit count is not a contradiction.

nodes.label: Impeccable Doctor Command
nodes.rationale: This is maintenance, not design. Do not redesign anything, do not open files outside the ones the report names, and do not run any other command as a side effect.

nodes.label: Schema Drift
nodes.rationale: Mechanical, and this command repairs most of it.

nodes.label: Truth Drift
nodes.rationale: No file comparison settles this.

nodes.label: workspace-context-inherited Finding
nodes.rationale: Inheritance is a designed behavior.

nodes.label: workspace-platform-native-evidence Finding
nodes.rationale: One inherited record cannot hold two platforms.

nodes.label: impeccable context Command
nodes.rationale: Restores missing or stale hook entries only when local consent is accepted; shared config consent does not authorize the write.

nodes.label: impeccable detect Command
nodes.rationale: Manual scans use the same project filter config by default; --no-config gives a raw detector run.

nodes.label: impeccable hooks Command
nodes.rationale: All config writes go through this command so writes stay validated and the file shape stays consistent.

nodes.label: Cursor
nodes.rationale: Cursor gets no Stop deep pass because its stop hook can only answer with a follow-up user message, so it keeps the full detector per edit.

nodes.label: Design Detector Hook
nodes.rationale: The hook never blocks an edit; it emits a post-edit reminder, and every hook is a mechanical pass whose reflexes no scanner catches live in craft-floor.md.

nodes.label: detector.extensions Config Field
nodes.rationale: Server-side template extensions must be declared because they sit outside the built-in extension list and the hook skips them otherwise; config only adds extensions, the built-in list always applies.

nodes.label: Gemini
nodes.rationale: Gemini installs session and completion hooks but no per-edit detector hook; on Windows no session id reaches the shell so the completion reminder stays silent.

nodes.label: GitHub Copilot
nodes.rationale: Copilot stop-style events do not feed context back to the model, so it keeps the full detector per edit.

nodes.label: Grok Build
nodes.rationale: Grok discards per-edit stdout, so findings surface on Stop additionalContext; the observe-only shutdown Stop is skipped.

nodes.label: Hermes Agent
nodes.rationale: Per-edit findings arrive inside the write_file or patch tool result as its impeccable field; the plugin sends the Stop event from pre_verify.

nodes.label: hook.consent Config Field
nodes.rationale: Per-developer install consent lives in the gitignored local config; without local consent context writes no manifests.

nodes.label: hook.perEditRules Config Field
nodes.rationale: Set to "all" to restore the full rule set on every edit instead of the immediate tier only.

nodes.label: impeccable-disable Inline Marker
nodes.rationale: Inline waivers are used only when the waiver must travel with a single file that leaves the repo; config ignores are preferred because they keep suppressions in one reviewable place.

nodes.label: MANUAL_DETECTOR_REQUIRED Directive
nodes.rationale: A session with no automatic hook gets one directive from impeccable context asking for a single detector run at the end.

nodes.label: Per-Edit Hook Pass
nodes.rationale: Surfaces only the immediate tier of mechanical, unambiguous problems worth interrupting an edit for; everything else is deferred to the Stop deep pass.

nodes.label: Stop Deep Pass
nodes.rationale: Runs the full rule set over every UI file touched in the session and surfaces remaining findings once, deduplicated against the per-edit pass, so a session with nothing left to report stops silently.

nodes.label: .impeccable/config.json
nodes.rationale: Unified Impeccable config: hook runtime settings under the hook key, shared detector ignores under detector.

nodes.label: .impeccable/config.local.json
nodes.rationale: Gitignored per-developer overrides, including the install consent decision the CLI records.

nodes.label: engine-checksums.txt
nodes.rationale: The launcher checks a downloaded engine against this file before its first run.

nodes.label: Throughput Checkpoint
nodes.rationale: A dimension that genuinely does not apply (single file, no fan-out) keeps its item with 'n/a: <reason>' rather than being dropped, so the checkpoint stays auditable.

nodes.label: Performance Mantras
nodes.rationale: Ordered cheapest first (don't do it, don't do it again, do it less, do it later, do it when they're not looking, do it concurrently, do it cheaper) so the least invasive fix that meets the target wins.

nodes.label: sequence-verifiable-units Principle Skill
nodes.rationale: Verify each unit before the next instead of batching checks at the end.

nodes.label: Feature Playbook
nodes.rationale: Delegating code-writing to a subagent is mandatory: no skip-with-reason escape, and the Laziness Protocol does not override it — the gain is review separation, not lines saved. A subagent forbidden to spawn satisfies this by owning the diff directly with the same review separation.

nodes.label: Hillclimb Playbook
nodes.rationale: Core discipline: one change, one measurement, keep or revert. Never stack untested changes, and never claim a win from code inspection. The stop predicate pairs a target with a floor on attempts so a lucky early win cannot end the run.

nodes.label: Investigation Playbook
nodes.rationale: Investigation requests are read-only: they produce a cited explanation or recommendation, not a code change, so no PR, babysit, or architect step applies.

nodes.label: Multi-phase or Multi-PR Plan Playbook
nodes.rationale: The plan is the deliverable, not the code. Tests alone are not sufficient verification: a PR is verified only when its unit, live, and perf boxes are all checked.

nodes.label: Opening a PR Playbook
nodes.rationale: Work from a git worktree off trunk to keep unrelated work out of the PR; the body is a one-minute briefing under 40 lines so reviewers get the essentials without a diff dump.

nodes.label: Pause Safely Playbook
nodes.rationale: Leave a checkpoint a cold-start agent can resume from; take no irreversible action to pause, and write the resume note off-context so compaction does not lose it.

nodes.label: Perf Issue Playbook
nodes.rationale: Tie every fix to a measurement rather than reading source instead of measuring; performance mantras are tried cheapest first and the loop stops as soon as an earlier mantra meets the target.

nodes.label: Prototype Playbook
nodes.rationale: The one playbook where the Laziness Protocol's 'smallest change' and the verification bar invert: speed over polish, code quality does not matter, and the rigor goes into picking the right design cheaply. The prototype is a throwaway instrument, not shippable code.

nodes.label: arena skill
nodes.rationale: Used when the implementation admits multiple valid shapes so the runners surface the alternatives and the cross-judge guards the pick.

nodes.label: scripts/check-pstack-pin.mjs
nodes.rationale: Fails when an installed pstack file differs from the mirror, when @mastra/code-sdk is not exact, or when a local patch mechanism exists.

nodes.label: CommandCode custom provider
nodes.rationale: Added to the existing settings using the COMMANDCODE_API_KEY already on the machine; the key is not printed or stored in the repository.

nodes.label: mastracode 0.47.1
nodes.rationale: The Mastra Code program is the separate package `mastracode`, not `@mastra/code-sdk`; it declares `@mastra/code-sdk: ^1.14.0` and is installed with that dependency pinned to 1.14.0.

nodes.label: pstack (backnotprop/pstack 0.15.32)
nodes.rationale: Three extra trees (Benny automation skills, docs/, README.md, LICENSE) were copied from the same commit because the documented install does not copy them.

nodes.label: gate.mjs
nodes.rationale: The gate rule lives in exactly one place, gate.mjs, so the merge decision cannot drift.

nodes.label: land.mjs
nodes.rationale: The merge is left to the forge (gh pr merge --squash --match-head-commit) so branch protection stays the thing that enforces the checks; --delete-branch is avoided because it deletes the local branch too and fails on any checkout holding it, making a successful merge read as a fault.

nodes.label: sweep.mjs
nodes.rationale: Sweep removes only what this card left behind: it never touches main, never touches a branch whose commits main does not hold, refuses anything under docs/scorecards/ so the cost rows stay, and never removes its own run folder.

nodes.label: scripts/mastra-program.mjs
nodes.rationale: Finds the global npm install of the Mastra Code program unless MASTRACODE_PROGRAM_DIR names another copy, so the Mastra modules are loaded from the installed program.

nodes.label: Shipping verdict gate rule
nodes.rationale: The machine does not judge the change and does not trust a local artifact: it takes the newest `Shipping agent:` comment for this card and pull request and lands only when the verdict is PASS or PASS+NOTES and the judged commit is the commit the branch points at now, because the branch moved after the review otherwise.

nodes.label: run record (record.json)
nodes.rationale: Every step saves the run record before handing on so a crash leaves finished steps recorded and a rerun continues instead of merging twice.

nodes.label: checks step
nodes.rationale: Reads the rollup first and waits because branch protection refuses a merge until the pull request's checks are done and a refusal reads like a fault; SUCCESS/NEUTRAL/SKIPPED are green, FAILURE stops the run, and a check that never finishes stops it after fifteen minutes.

nodes.label: ci step
nodes.rationale: The machine does not merge behind a red main; red ends the run, the reason goes on the card and the card stays in progress for remediation.

nodes.label: complete step
nodes.rationale: A comment already carrying that commit is not written twice.

nodes.label: metrics step
nodes.rationale: Landing facts go beside the scorecard in a .landing.json because docs/scorecards/<CARD>.md is generated by scripts/scorecard.mjs and would overwrite anything appended to it.

nodes.label: publish step
nodes.rationale: Main is protected by a ruleset requiring checks, so nothing is pushed straight at it; the landing facts and the retro land in one merge so the record and the retro it describes are never out of step, and the pull request names no card because a pull request that names one must also carry that card's scorecard.

nodes.label: Mastra workflow `merge`
nodes.rationale: Built as the stock Mastra workflow with nine steps so each step saves the run record before handing on; a crash leaves finished steps in record.json and a rerun continues from there instead of merging twice.

nodes.label: docs/scorecards/<CARD>.landing.json
nodes.rationale: Holds the landing facts (card duration and review rounds with verdicts) beside the generated scorecard so they are not overwritten.

nodes.label: findBuilderThread
nodes.rationale: Reads the session store and takes the newest thread in this project whose title or own user turn names the card, so the failure goes back to the session that built the change.

nodes.label: /arena skill
nodes.rationale: Repeats one design or code brief, then picks a base and grafts the best parts; cheap next to a design that is expensive to reverse.

nodes.label: /benchmark-checklist skill
nodes.rationale: A warm cache or skipped code path can fake a speedup, so numbers are vetted before they go anywhere.

nodes.label: /bro skill
nodes.rationale: Restates the last message like one human talking to another, no jargon, shorter, for replies that are technically thorough but unclear.

nodes.label: /correct skill
nodes.rationale: A correction in chat helps one run; /correct lands the fix in the repo as architecture, a type, a lint, or a test so no later run repeats it.

nodes.label: /in-your-own-words skill
nodes.rationale: Asks for a restatement alone, with no playbook, so a misreading surfaces cheaply.

nodes.label: /interrogate skill
nodes.rationale: Keeps only findings a rerun proves and lists what it dropped and why, filtering bot and human noise.

nodes.label: /ketchup skill
nodes.rationale: Reports what changed since the last message and lists each call waiting on the user with pick, evidence, and risk; changes nothing while it reports.

nodes.label: /ketchup-video skill
nodes.rationale: Shows the catch-up as a short subtitled video of slides with the waiting calls listed as text under it.

nodes.label: /loop skill
nodes.rationale: A loop that cannot verify its own work only makes unchecked work faster, so the verification skill must work first.

nodes.label: /poteto-help skill
nodes.rationale: Answers with an answer, a prompt to send, and a link to the source; nothing runs until the prompt is sent.

nodes.label: /sharpen skill
nodes.rationale: Rewrites the prompt to ask for expert-level work but does not perform the task, so the user sends the rewrite when it reads right.

nodes.label: swarm Skill
nodes.rationale: Independent verifiers fan out at the code-ready SHA because no lane trusts a claim it has not checked.

nodes.label: 08-principles.md
nodes.rationale: Provides the vocabulary of steering prompt names.

nodes.label: Authoring or modifying a skill playbook
nodes.norm_label: authoring or modifying a skill playbook
nodes.rationale: Writing a SKILL.md freehand skips validation and review, so authoring is routed through this playbook.

nodes.label: Eval Playbook
nodes.rationale: You own the experiment design: blinding is non-negotiable so the candidate prompt looks like an organic user request, and chain-following is graded from transcripts and code shape rather than self-report.

nodes.label: Flaky tests
nodes.rationale: A deterministic step failing every run at the same place with the same code is a product bug or a changed screen, not a flake.

nodes.label: --no-cache
nodes.rationale: A failed run already deletes the replay that ran into the failure, so rerun with the cache on first.

nodes.label: screen.pause()
nodes.rationale: Paused time doesn't count toward any timeout.

nodes.label: .e2e/ output directory
nodes.rationale: Output only — read it, never edit it; the config's output moves the report and artifacts but never cache/ or the app log.

nodes.label: trace page
nodes.rationale: The trace records every step, app log, agent turn and the screen at failure, so a failure is fixed from evidence instead of re-walking the flow.

nodes.label: e2e explore
nodes.rationale: Runs the agent against the app with a goal instead of a test file, so an app can be explored before tests exist, regressions hunted on a branch, or candidate tests discovered. Needs only a config with a target and an agent holding a model.

nodes.label: report_finding tool
nodes.rationale: The agent reports each defect the moment it has evidence: title, issue or warning, severity 1 to 5, expected, actual, reproduction steps; the runner adds the path and a redacted screenshot.

nodes.label: StepExecutor
nodes.rationale: A hand-rolled StepExecutor under executor is replaced by the built-in agent for the run, with a notice on stderr, and needs a model on the entry (or the executor's) or explore fails before it starts.

nodes.label: type_secret tool
nodes.rationale: Offered only when the engine can fill secrets; otherwise the agent skips signing in and says so in the step summary.

nodes.label: app.bundleId
nodes.rationale: Explore installs no build, so a local device target needs app.bundleId; an appPath alone leaves nothing to launch.

nodes.label: Attempt directory
nodes.rationale: The slug is the goal's first words in lowercase ASCII, capped, and the id keeps distinct goals, targets, and agents apart while the same goal on the same target and agent always maps to the same directory.

nodes.label: --changed-since
nodes.rationale: Only a defect the change can cause is an issue; one elsewhere is a warning. The planner may skip a change no user can see, such as docs or tests only, and that run ends skipped and passes.

nodes.label: CONFIG_NOT_FOUND
nodes.rationale: Without a terminal for the init wizard (an agent's shell, CI), explore fails with CONFIG_NOT_FOUND, so npx e2e init --yes must run first.

nodes.label: Configured credentials
nodes.rationale: Reach the explorer as step secrets: the planner knows the account names and usernames, and the agent fills passwords with type_secret by name. Only configured secrets are redacted.

nodes.label: Explorer agent
nodes.rationale: Built from a configured agent (agents.<name>); the entry's tools and system carry over, but a hand-rolled StepExecutor under executor is replaced by the built-in agent for the run.

nodes.label: Findings
nodes.rationale: Findings are the model's claims plus evidence, not verified reproductions: read actual against the screenshot before filing a bug.

nodes.label: Planner
nodes.rationale: A structured model call reads the goal, the steps and findings so far, and the current screen, and answers with a title and a concrete charter for one flow, or decides the goal is covered.

nodes.label: --session / sessions
nodes.rationale: Starts the exploration from a session a setup test saves, so no charter is spent signing in again.

nodes.label: GitLab CI
nodes.rationale: On GitLab, pass --changed-since ${CI_MERGE_REQUEST_TARGET_BRANCH_SHA:-$CI_MERGE_REQUEST_DIFF_BASE_SHA} on merge request pipelines, not merge trains, with GIT_DEPTH: 0.

nodes.label: GitHub CLI (gh)
nodes.rationale: gh is the default forge; Graphite (gt) is never required.

nodes.label: Origin forge CLI (origin pr)
nodes.rationale: Preferred over gh when `command -v origin` succeeds and Origin can resolve the repository.

nodes.label: Verify the Result and Open a PR
nodes.norm_label: verify the result and open a pr
nodes.rationale: Verification is the slowest step in most agent work because it usually waits on a human; make the agent able to do it and you stop being the bottleneck, otherwise more agents only produce more unchecked work.

nodes.label: /create-formal-verification-skill
nodes.rationale: Targets bugs on paths nobody drives (overlapping retries, locks expiring mid-write, out-of-order state changes); it picks the strongest target, not the easiest to verify, and shows the property failing on a broken variant because a check you've never seen fail proves nothing.

nodes.label: /create-verification-skill
nodes.rationale: Interviews the repository rather than the user to work out how the app launches, what can drive it, and what evidence proves behavior, then proves the generated skill once end to end before handing it over.

nodes.label: /maintain-formal-verification-skill
