nodes.rationale: Merges and refactors that skip the skill can leave a check passing on a description of code that's gone, so the verification is updated from the code and each updated check is shown to still be able to fail.

nodes.label: /maintain-verification-skill
nodes.rationale: Feature maps go out of date; the audit never edits product code and reports a product regression instead of hiding it with a doc edit.

nodes.label: Build the Lever Principle
nodes.rationale: When agents keep writing throwaway scripts to click through the app, a small control CLI makes runs repeatable and spends fewer tokens.

nodes.label: Prove It Works Principle
nodes.rationale: "It compiles" is not evidence; the agent must check the real artifact before reporting success.

nodes.label: create-formal-verification-skill skill
nodes.rationale: A test checks the cases someone thought to write; formal verification checks every case in a stated scope, so the target is the promise where a break harms users and tests rarely reach the breaking case.

nodes.label: Shipping Playbook
nodes.rationale: Only a verdict from an agent that did not write the code counts, because an author checks what it meant to build; green CI and an approving bot review are not verdicts because neither runs the change as a user would.

nodes.label: /blast-radius
nodes.rationale: Finds the one fact that makes a small diff safe and proves that fact by running code, not by arguing for it.

nodes.label: Worked Feature-Map Example
nodes.rationale: A README index plus one file per feature using the four required H2s, shipped with the verification skill generator.

nodes.label: Babysit Playbook
nodes.rationale: Takes blockers in order (conflicts, then review threads, then CI) and never rebases or force-pushes; it stops at merge-ready because merging is a different decision.

nodes.label: Shipping Playbook
nodes.rationale: Green is not the same as safe: one fresh agent per PR proves the behavior live, the agent that judges a change is never the one that wrote it, and only the contiguous verified run lands from the bottom.

nodes.label: Visual Parity Playbook
nodes.rationale: Diffs screenshots against a frozen baseline instead of judging by eye when output must match a reference pixel for pixel.

nodes.label: /statechart
nodes.rationale: Draws the statechart from the TLA+ model so the picture and the checked model can't drift apart, and reproduces each bug path in the real code so a modeling error doesn't reach the reader as a bug.

nodes.label: Verification Illustration (prototype plane on a test course)
nodes.norm_label: verification illustration (prototype plane on a test course)

nodes.label: ai (Vercel AI SDK v7)
nodes.rationale: Only needed for agent.* steps.

nodes.label: decisionFilter()
nodes.rationale: Runs only the tests a pull request can affect, and relevance makes each target start the likeliest files first.

nodes.label: e2e.config.ts
nodes.rationale: Sits at the project root and default-exports an object literal ending in `satisfies E2EConfig` so unknown keys are rejected as INVALID_CONFIG at load.

nodes.label: gateway()
nodes.rationale: Without AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY, gateway() uses a Vercel OIDC token.

nodes.label: cache.strict
nodes.rationale: Must be off when re-recording stale entries before committing.

nodes.label: REPLAY_STALE
nodes.rationale: Raised by --strict-cache when a committed recording no longer replays; re-record with a read-write run without the flag and with cache.strict off, then commit.

nodes.label: --strict-cache
nodes.rationale: In CI with committed recordings, fails a recording that no longer replays with REPLAY_STALE instead of quietly spending model calls every run.

nodes.label: agents config key
nodes.rationale: Tests run with `default` and entries never inherit from `default`, so each named agent is self-contained.

nodes.label: cache config key
nodes.rationale: `strict` fails a step whose recording no longer replays instead of handing it to the agent, and the run never writes the cache.

nodes.label: credentials config key
nodes.rationale: A string password is checked at load (6+ code points) so a missing env var fails early rather than at fill time.

nodes.label: environment variables the runner reads
nodes.rationale: E2E_USER_<NAME>_* and E2E_SECRET_<NAME> override config entries so CI can supply values without editing the config.

nodes.label: filters config key
nodes.rationale: Read files, environment, or network inside `filter`, never at config load, because workers load the config too.

nodes.label: output config key
nodes.rationale: Must be inside the project root but not the root, not a tests glob's directory, and never the cache dir.

nodes.label: projectId config key
nodes.rationale: Report and cache identity; defaults to the package name.

nodes.label: secrets config key
nodes.rationale: A separate namespace from credentials so a name may exist in both; the model never sees secret values.

nodes.label: tests glob config key
nodes.rationale: Discovery enters only directories a glob can match and symlinks are not followed; exclusions-only globs are INVALID_CONFIG.

nodes.label: trace config key
nodes.rationale: Works on every engine; neither trace nor video invalidates the replay cache.

nodes.label: video config key
nodes.rationale: A config or flag mode skips targets whose engine cannot record (one notice), while a target or test mode requires it (UNSUPPORTED_ARTIFACT).

nodes.label: @e2e-dev/web
nodes.rationale: Pins playwright-core exactly; do not add playwright for it.

nodes.label: e2e init wizard
nodes.rationale: The wizard picks engines and a model provider and offers to install the skill, register the MCP server, and install dependencies; --yes picks web engine plus Vercel AI Gateway and skips dependency installation so an agent shell can run it non-interactively.

nodes.label: kernel()
nodes.rationale: On a headed hosted browser use viewport null and size the service's screen; a fixed size gives a smaller, unmaximized window.

nodes.label: lightpanda()
nodes.rationale: Worker scope only.

nodes.label: moli()
nodes.rationale: Worker scope only.

nodes.label: notte()
nodes.rationale: Attempt scope only.

nodes.label: testmuBrowsers()
nodes.rationale: Worker scope only.

nodes.label: web() engine
nodes.rationale: chromiumSandbox defaults to true on macOS and Windows and false on Linux, where root and most containers cannot start it.

nodes.label: APP_ALREADY_RUNNING
nodes.rationale: A run beside a session on a fixed port without reuseExisting fails; offer the user reuseExisting: true, never add it unasked.

nodes.label: APP_UNREACHABLE
nodes.rationale: Occurs when the app stops under a run, e.g. a session that started the app closes during the run, or a dev server allows one copy per directory.

nodes.label: Web Target app Config
nodes.rationale: Whether a session can stay open during e2e run depends on the target's app: no command, a url on port 0, a command on a fixed port with or without reuseExisting.

nodes.label: app.command
nodes.rationale: Prefer app.command to a hand-started dev server: self-contained locally and in CI. The child gets only a minimal environment so model keys and E2E_USER_* values are never inherited unless named in inheritEnv.

nodes.label: app.url
nodes.rationale: Port 0 on 127.0.0.1 or [::1] takes a free port, expanded as {port} in args, env, and readyUrl.

nodes.label: MCP server registration
nodes.rationale: Re-running init preserves the server's environment and client settings while repairing its launch command; a current registration is left unchanged.

nodes.label: Next.js integration
nodes.rationale: A Next.js 16 dev server blocks cross-origin requests to its dev resources, so a 127.0.0.1 target never hydrates unless the host is added to allowedDevOrigins.

nodes.label: OPERATION_TIMEOUT
nodes.rationale: Recovery never repeats a dispatched operation; exhausting the budget is OPERATION_TIMEOUT.

nodes.label: e2e skill installation
nodes.rationale: When the client already has the e2e plugin, pass --skills none, since the plugin gives it the skill.

nodes.label: targets config key
nodes.rationale: Required and non-empty; UI targets set engine and app, tools-only targets may omit engine but must set platform.

nodes.label: app.open
nodes.rationale: In a browser every test starts from a fresh context with no page open, so it calls app.open() first; on a device a test that skips app.open() starts where the previous test left the app.

nodes.label: browser.cookies()
nodes.rationale: A declared session is restored before fixtures run, so when the app signs in with a cookie, browser.cookies() signs the fixture's requests in.

nodes.label: device.openLink()
nodes.rationale: On a device there are no sessions; without app.linkBase, device.openLink() opens a route or a sign-in link in the app.

nodes.label: app.linkBase
nodes.rationale: app.open() takes a path only on a target with app.linkBase, e.g. linkBase: 'myapp://' makes app.open('/projects/42') open myapp://projects/42.

nodes.label: observe over MCP
nodes.rationale: observe over MCP prints the path of the screen you reached, which tells you what to pass to app.open().

nodes.label: project fixture
nodes.rationale: Seeds a project through the API and deletes it afterwards, which runs after a failure too.

nodes.label: session fixture
nodes.rationale: Restores state saved by a setup test.

nodes.label: session.save
nodes.rationale: A setup test's session.save is bookkeeping and comes after its check.

nodes.label: test.extend
nodes.rationale: Code after use() is teardown, runs after failures too; a test.extend() chain registers hooks that see its fixtures through test.beforeEach.

nodes.label: test.setup
nodes.rationale: Must be top-level, outside any describe; a setup test cannot skip from its body (INVALID_ARGUMENT) and cannot call test.fail.

nodes.label: Sign-in Sessions
nodes.rationale: Only the setup fills the sign-in form; a session lasts one run, so the setup runs once per target for all selected tests that declare its session.

nodes.label: Start Near the Screen Under Test
nodes.norm_label: start near the screen under test
nodes.rationale: A test pays for every step before the screen it checks on every run and every rerun; a wrong locator at the end of a long flow reruns the whole flow and then waits out the 30 s action timeout.

nodes.label: DESIGN.md frontmatter token schema
nodes.rationale: Tokens are normative; prose provides context for how to apply them.

nodes.label: .impeccable/design.json sidecar
nodes.rationale: Carries what Stitch's schema can't hold: tonal ramps, shadow/elevation tokens, motion tokens, breakpoints, full component HTML/CSS snippets, and narrative.

nodes.label: DESIGN.md
nodes.rationale: Captures the current visual design system so AI agents generating new screens stay on-brand.

nodes.label: dashboard/config/roles.json
nodes.rationale: Specific models live in the pstack models file or settings, never in docs.

nodes.label: machine/guards/guard.test.mjs
nodes.rationale: Holds one planted violation per rule so a weakened guard rule fails its own test.

nodes.label: Retro skill
nodes.rationale: After a slice merges, retro fixes go in one PR with a plain-English list for Todd to approve.

nodes.label: Adversarial review
nodes.rationale: A review by an agent other than the builder that tries to break the work rather than confirm it.

nodes.label: Front door
nodes.rationale: The only way into Julia; there is no public part.

nodes.label: Household
nodes.rationale: There is exactly one household; every piece of data in Julia belongs to it, never to an individual.

nodes.label: Household account
nodes.rationale: Julia never distinguishes between the two accepted Google accounts.

nodes.label: Journey
nodes.rationale: The unit the spec is written in and the unit Todd accepts.

nodes.label: Parking lot
nodes.rationale: Read at every retro and at each milestone boundary.

nodes.label: Plan
nodes.rationale: Approved automatically and saved in the pull request; both reviewers check the work against it.

nodes.label: Shipping verdict
nodes.rationale: CI stays red without a PASS on the pull request's current head.

nodes.label: locator.waitFor
nodes.rationale: Ending an arrange block with a wait makes a setup goal that passed without doing its job fail there, not at the outcome check, and confirms the setup goals for the replay cache.

nodes.label: agent.act
nodes.rationale: Goals are atomic — one outcome confirmed by one check — so a failing goal identifies exactly what broke.

nodes.label: agent.waitFor
nodes.rationale: Preferred over sleeps or fixed delays: wait for the state you need instead of a timeout.

nodes.label: Cache Entry Key
nodes.rationale: Holds the test file and title path, the target, the instruction and params, the agent, its context, and the test's agentContext, so renaming the test or its file records every goal in it again, and rewording a goal records that goal again.

nodes.label: Cache Modes (read-write, read-only, off)
nodes.rationale: On by default (read-write), read-only in CI, off via cache: 'off' or --no-cache; CI stays read-only unless cache: 'read-write' is set.

nodes.label: Hand-off to Live Agent
nodes.rationale: When the app or final state no longer matches, the live agent continues from the current screen; misses and hand-offs use the model.

nodes.label: MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED
nodes.rationale: A failure where no model answered implicates nothing and evicts nothing.

nodes.label: no-change
nodes.rationale: A step changing nothing on screen or in the route creates no entry and runs live every run; a change only inside a frame from another site counts as nothing, since the tree leaves it out.

nodes.label: param-collision
nodes.rationale: A step whose unique() value equals, is spelled inside, or is the encoded form of another param's value is not recorded.

nodes.label: step.cache.notRecorded
nodes.rationale: A step whose unique() value equals, is spelled inside, or is the encoded form of another param's value is not recorded (param-collision).

nodes.label: step.cache.reason
nodes.rationale: Explains why a replay did not happen: no-entry, wrong-context, target-not-found, target-ambiguous, end-mismatch, and so on.

nodes.label: step.cache.recordedBy
nodes.rationale: Replay reports expose the original model when available; older recordings omit it, so --no-cache is used to evaluate a new model.

nodes.label: step.cache.write
nodes.rationale: A step changing nothing on screen or in the route creates no entry (no-change) and runs live every run, strict included.

nodes.label: CI mode
nodes.rationale: On when CI is set (not 0 or false): retries 1, workers 1, test.only rejected, replay cache read-only unless the config sets a mode explicitly, reuseExisting ignored.

nodes.label: replay cache
nodes.rationale: Goals confirmed by a later check or wait are recorded and replayed without model calls, so reruns of a failing test stay cheap; only read-write cache mode records.

nodes.label: impeccable context
nodes.rationale: Setup runs as for any command: impeccable context, this reference, and craft-floor.md before the edit.

nodes.label: impeccable live-complete
nodes.rationale: Completes the session after the accept cleanup and confirms phase: completed.

nodes.label: impeccable live-generate
nodes.rationale: One command boots the helper, hands the element to the overlay in the page the harness already shows, and returns the generate event.

nodes.label: impeccable live-poll
nodes.rationale: Replies done (the browser mounts the variants) and then blocks until the user's choice arrives, so the harness wakes the agent when it returns.

nodes.label: impeccable live-resume
nodes.rationale: Resumes a session after live-status when the state is uncertain.

nodes.label: impeccable live-server stop
nodes.rationale: Stopping removes the injected script and reloads the page once; the dev server is never killed or restarted.

nodes.label: impeccable live-status
nodes.rationale: Used when interrupted or unsure of the state; the journal under .impeccable/live/sessions/ is canonical.

nodes.label: Boot
nodes.rationale: Boot loads PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md again for the helper, tolerates missing files, finds the dev URL, hides the bottom bar for the helper's lifetime, and reuses a helper that is already running.

nodes.label: Generate Command
nodes.rationale: The lane's plumbing is where time is saved (one command starts the session, one call replies and waits); the design work is not, so variants are planned, written and accepted exactly as in a live session.

nodes.label: Generate Event
nodes.rationale: The event carries the picked element's context, a preflighted scaffold, and _instructions naming the action's reference, the planning section, and the exact splice; verdict _instructions win over recollection of this file.

nodes.label: Preflighted Scaffold
nodes.rationale: The preview CSS plus every variant are written in one edit at the scaffold's splice.

nodes.label: Session ID
nodes.rationale: Only the browser mints session ids (8 hex characters, at Go); a missing event is fixed by rerunning Step 2, never with a direct source edit.

nodes.label: Step 1: Parse the Request
nodes.rationale: Three parts must be held before continuing: an action from the vocabulary, a count from 1 to 8 (default 3, protocol caps at 8), and the element description.

nodes.label: Step 2: Reuse the Page, Then Start
nodes.norm_label: step 2: reuse the page, then start
nodes.rationale: Reuse the dev server already running and the tab the harness already shows; a second server or a second browser window is the failure this step prevents.

nodes.label: Step 3: Generate
nodes.rationale: The event is a standard generate event handled exactly per live.md's Handle generate; the lane changes nothing about what a variant may be.

nodes.label: Step 4: Accept and Close
nodes.rationale: Close without being asked the moment the choice is handled; stopping the helper removes the injected script and reloads once so the user sees the accepted design with no overlay chrome.

nodes.label: Generate Reference (live mode fast lane)
nodes.rationale: Generate is the fast lane into live mode: one command boots the helper, hands the element to the overlay, one edit writes the variants, one call replies and waits for the user's choice, which the helper bakes into source itself.

nodes.label: DESIGN.md
nodes.rationale: When DESIGN.md exists the start command prints it under boot and it is used; when it does not, the identity is extracted from the event instead of interviewing the user.

nodes.label: PRODUCT.md
nodes.rationale: When PRODUCT.md exists the start command prints it under boot and it is used; when it does not, the identity is extracted from the event instead of interviewing the user.

nodes.label: Optimize Reference
nodes.rationale: Performance is a feature. Identify the actual bottleneck for THIS interface, fix it, then measure. Don't optimize what isn't slow.

nodes.label: --agent flag
nodes.rationale: Runs the suite as any configured agent, comparing candidates on the same tests; every result records which agent ran it.

nodes.label: defineTool
nodes.rationale: Adds AI SDK tools wrapped with defineTool(tool({ ... }), { mutates: true }) for a test API a flow calls mid-step.

nodes.label: gateway()
nodes.rationale: The config's model reads the key passed via env: { AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY } for gateway().

nodes.label: AI Trace
nodes.rationale: Never read the trace directly: megabytes of resent context, images replaced by byte counts.

nodes.label: E2E cache
nodes.rationale: Sharing .e2e/cache/ lets CI replay verified action steps without model calls.

nodes.label: e2e init
nodes.rationale: Gitignores .e2e/cache/ by default; removing that line lets entries be committed and shared.

nodes.label: Recorder
nodes.rationale: The recorder redacts serialized tool results and errors before writing the AI trace.

nodes.label: AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY
nodes.rationale: Pass the key the config's model reads (AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY for gateway() from ai) as a secret in the run step's env.

nodes.label: critique-storage close
nodes.rationale: Closes only the snapshot this pass actually processed; if a newer critique landed meanwhile, its backlog stays live. Do not close when no snapshot was read, when snapshot_file was not retained, or when Priority Issues remain.

nodes.label: critique-storage latest
nodes.rationale: Exit 0 returns JSON with the latest snapshot's body and an exact snapshot_file identity; exit 2 means none exists or the target changed.

nodes.label: impeccable context
nodes.rationale: Context requests a manual scan only when no automatic detector is active; never add another detector pass.

nodes.label: Quality Bar
nodes.rationale: They set the craft level the build must reach, a rendered reference's finish, commitment, and art direction, never the composition.

nodes.label: Conceptual Mismatch
nodes.rationale: The flow, information architecture, or hierarchy differs from comparable product areas.

nodes.label: Detector Result
nodes.rationale: A detector result is defect evidence, not proof of quality; a clean scan does not replace visual judgment.

nodes.label: Establish the System
nodes.rationale: Fix the cause at the narrowest correct level; ask when a binding system principle cannot be inferred.

nodes.label: Local Defect
nodes.rationale: The implementation is simply incomplete or inconsistent.

nodes.label: Missing Token
nodes.rationale: The system needs a reusable value.

nodes.label: One-off Implementation
nodes.rationale: An existing shared component or pattern should replace it.

nodes.label: Source Diff
nodes.rationale: Remove accidental churn, orphaned code, redundant values, and temporary artifacts before shipping.

nodes.label: Polish Reference
nodes.rationale: Polish is refinement, never concealed redesign. Preserve the incumbent visual world, content, behavior, and everything outside scope; if the concept itself is wrong, recommend redesign or bolder instead of smuggling in a replacement.

nodes.label: Migrate to e2e Skill
nodes.rationale: A migration is never one change; each session ports one slice, proves it, and leaves both suites green, with MIGRATION.md preserving state for later sessions.

nodes.label: MIGRATION.md Progress File
nodes.rationale: Records what moved, what is left, and why, so the next session starts from it instead of from scratch.

nodes.label: Blast Radius
nodes.rationale: Smoke the blast radius around the changed behavior; stop without a pull request if a regression remains.

nodes.label: Bounded Fix
nodes.rationale: Fix the root cause with the smallest justified change; stop if the change grows beyond the configured effort or risk budget.

nodes.label: Draft Pull Request
nodes.rationale: Only after before-and-after proof; never merge or deploy from this workflow.

nodes.label: Repro Evidence
nodes.rationale: A compile, unit test, code review, or plausible diff is not after evidence.

nodes.label: Operations Thread
nodes.rationale: The only allowed root post in the repro workflow; never substitute a source-channel root message.

nodes.label: Reproduction
nodes.rationale: The exact discriminating symptom must appear twice through real UI interaction; state inspection may confirm but must not inject the symptom.

nodes.label: Root Cause Analysis
nodes.rationale: Confirm the mechanism with runtime evidence and eliminate competing hypotheses before editing.

nodes.label: Hard Safety Rules
nodes.rationale: The coordinator is the only Slack poster; delegated workers are read-only and must be denied Slack credentials and write actions.

nodes.label: Frozen Source Coordinates
nodes.rationale: Never replace these values with a reply timestamp, operations timestamp, or status-message timestamp.

nodes.label: Triage Marker Contract
nodes.rationale: The marker replaces private bot identities and free-form verdict matching.

nodes.label: Verify Existing Fix Mode
nodes.rationale: Existing pull requests or commits switch the run to verify mode; do not author over them.

nodes.label: Reproduce and Fix Issues Skill
nodes.rationale: Reproduce triaged Slack bugs through a configured app-control adapter, verify existing fixes, and open a bounded draft pull request only after before-and-after proof; use only from the configured Benny repro automation.
